questions.question: In the context of India's pre-1991 economic structure, which of the following best characterizes the contradiction between sectoral GDP contribution and employment absorption?

options.text: Services led GDP growth and employment generation equally
Manufacturing became the primary employment generator
Industry contributed the most to GDP and employment
Agriculture contributed declining GDP share but absorbed majority employment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture contributed declining GDP share but absorbed majority employment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The structural transformation of the Indian economy between **1950** and **1991** was unique and contradictory compared to global development patterns. In a typical developing economy, labor moves from **Agriculture** to **Industry** and then to **Services**.
 
• While the share of **Agriculture** in the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** declined significantly—from about **50%** in **1950-51** to around **30%** by **1990-91**—the proportion of the population dependent on it for a livelihood did not decline proportionately.
 
• During this period, the **Primary Sector (Agriculture)** continued to absorb the majority of the workforce, accounting for approximately **67.4%** of employment in **1991**, despite its falling contribution to the national income. **Hence, the statement regarding agriculture's declining GDP share vs. high employment absorption is correct.**
 
• The **Industrial Sector** failed to grow at a pace rapid enough to absorb the surplus labor from the rural areas. Even though the **Secondary Sector** grew under various **Five-Year Plans**, its capacity for **employment generation** remained limited. **Hence, the statement that manufacturing became the primary employment generator is incorrect.**
 
• The **Services Sector (Tertiary Sector)** saw a faster growth in **GDP** share than the industrial sector, but this growth was not accompanied by an equivalent increase in employment opportunities during the pre-reform era. **Hence, the statement that services led growth and employment equally is incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structural Composition of GDP:**

 
 
• At the time of independence in **1947**, India was a predominantly agrarian economy. The **Planning Commission** was established in **1950** to guide economic development.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)**, based on the **Mahalanobis Model**, focused heavily on heavy industries to modernize the economy, yet the workforce shift remained stagnant.
 
 
 
• **Disguised Unemployment:**
 
 
• The contradiction of high employment in **Agriculture** with low **GDP** contribution led to **Disguised Unemployment**. This is a phenomenon where more people are working in a sector than are actually required, and their marginal productivity is zero.
 
• By **1990**, while **Agriculture** contributed only about **one-third** of the **GDP**, it still supported **two-thirds** of the Indian population.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Secondary and Tertiary Sectors:**
 
 
• The **Secondary Sector** includes **Manufacturing**, **Electricity**, and **Construction**. Its share in **GDP** increased from **13%** in **1950** to about **24%** in **1990**.
 
• The **Tertiary Sector** (Trade, Transport, Banking, etc.) grew from **30%** to approximately **40%** of **GDP** in the same period, but the "jobless growth" in services became a point of concern for economists.
 
 
 
• **Economic Reforms of 1991:**
 
 
• Due to this structural imbalance and a **Balance of Payments (BoP)** crisis, India introduced **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** reforms in **July 1991** under the leadership of **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• Post-**1991**, the **Services Sector** became the main engine of **GDP** growth, though the challenge of shifting labor out of low-productivity agriculture remains a major theme in Indian economics today.

questions.question: A dealer buys two articles X and Y for ₹800 each. He marks each of them at the same price. He sells X by giving two successive discounts of 45% and 73% and still earns ₹523 as profit. If he sells Y at a single discount of 89%, then what is the profit percentage on Y?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SP of X = CP + Profit = 800 + 523 = 1323.

Remaining SP factor after 45% and 73% discounts = 0.55 × 0.27 = 0.1485.

Remaining SP factor after 89% discount = 0.11.

Ratio SPX : SPY = 0.1485 : 0.11 = 135 : 100 = 27 : 20.

27 units = 1323 ⇒ 1 unit = 49 ⇒ SPY = 20 × 49 = 980.

Profit % on Y = (980 − 800) ÷ 800 × 100 = 180 ÷ 8 = 22.5%.

**∴ Answer = 22.5%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

CP of X = CP of Y = 800. MP of X = MP of Y. Profit on X = 523. Discounts on X = 45%, 73%. Discount on Y = 89%.

**Formula used:**

SP = CP + Profit; SP = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100); Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100

 CP = 800 
• MP 
 X: 45%, 73% disc. SP_X = 1323 
 Y: 89% disc. SP_Y = 980 Profit on Y = 980 − 800 = 180 

**Calculations:**

For article X:

⇒ SPX = 800 + 523 = 1323

⇒ SPX = MP × (1 − 45/100) × (1 − 73/100)

⇒ 1323 = MP × 0.55 × 0.27

⇒ MP = 1323 ÷ (0.55 × 0.27) = 1323 ÷ 0.1485

For article Y:

⇒ SPY = MP × (1 − 89/100) = MP × 0.11

⇒ SPY = (1323 ÷ 0.1485) × 0.11 = 1323 × (1100 ÷ 1485)

⇒ SPY = 1323 × (20 ÷ 27) = 49 × 20 = 980

⇒ Profit on Y = 980 − 800 = 180

⇒ Profit % = (180 ÷ 800) × 100 = 22.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 22.5% (Option 2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

Two successive discounts of a% and b% are equivalent to a single discount of [a + b − (a × b)/100]%.

Marked Price Formula

MP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%). This relates CP and MP directly when profit and discount are known.

Effective Value

If an item is discounted by d%, its selling price becomes (100 − d)% of its marked price.

questions.question: Simplify: (732 times 732 times 732 + 268 times 268 times 268)/(73.2 times 73.2 + 26.8 times 26.8 - 73.2 times 26.8)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Expression is of the form (a³ + b³) / (x² + y² − xy) where a = 10x and b = 10y.

Numerator = (10x)³ + (10y)³ = 1000(x³ + y³).

Expression reduces to 1000 × (x³ + y³) / (x² − xy + y²) = 1000(x + y).

Substitute x = 73.2 and y = 26.8: 1000 × (73.2 + 26.8) = 1000 × 100 = 100000.

**∴ The correct answer is 100000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numerator = 732³ + 268³ and Denominator = 73.2² + 26.8² − 73.2 × 26.8

**Formula Used:** a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)

⇒ Let x = 73.2 and y = 26.8. Then 732 = 10x and 268 = 10y.

⇒ Expression = [(10x)³ + (10y)³] / [x² + y² − xy]

⇒ Expression = [1000x³ + 1000y³] / [x² − xy + y²]

⇒ Expression = 1000 × (x³ + y³) / (x² − xy + y²)

⇒ Expression = 1000 × [(x + y)(x² − xy + y²)] / (x² − xy + y²)

⇒ Expression = 1000 × (x + y)

⇒ Expression = 1000 × (73.2 + 26.8)

⇒ Expression = 1000 × 100 = 100000.

**∴ The correct answer is 100000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity: Sum of Cubes

The formula a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) is a standard identity used to simplify expressions where a cubic sum is divided by a quadratic term.

Algebraic Identity: Difference of Cubes

Similarly, a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) is used for simplifying subtractions of cubes.

Decimal and Power Relationship

If a number is multiplied by 10, its square is multiplied by 100 (10²) and its cube is multiplied by 1000 (10³).

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the three-tier structure of the Council of Ministers?

options.text: Chief Ministers – State Ministers – Deputy Chief Ministers
Cabinet Ministers – Ministers of State – Deputy Ministers
Prime Minister – Ministers of State – Cabinet Ministers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cabinet Ministers – Ministers of State – Deputy Ministers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Council of Ministers** in **India** consists of a three-tier hierarchy of ministers, which includes **Cabinet Ministers**, **Ministers of State**, and **Deputy Ministers**.
 
• **Cabinet Ministers**: These are the senior-most members of the **Council of Ministers**. They hold the charge of crucial ministries of the **Central Government** such as **Home**, **Defense**, **Finance**, and **External Affairs**. They are the primary policy-making body of the **Government of India**. *Hence, this tier is correctly identified.*
 
• **Ministers of State**: This is the second tier of the council. They can either be given **independent charge** of ministries/departments or can be attached to **Cabinet Ministers**. When attached, they assist the **Cabinet Ministers** in the discharge of their duties. *Hence, this tier is correctly identified.*
 
• **Deputy Ministers**: These are the third tier of the **Council of Ministers**. They are not given **independent charge** of any ministry and are always attached to **Cabinet Ministers** or **Ministers of State**. Their main function is to assist in administrative, parliamentary, and departmental work. *Hence, this tier is correctly identified.*
 
• The **Prime Minister** sits at the top of this entire structure as the head of the **Council of Ministers**, exercising supreme executive authority. *Hence, the statement representing the tiers as Cabinet, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Basis**: **Article 74** of the **Constitution of India** provides for a **Council of Ministers** with the **Prime Minister** at the head to aid and advise the **President**. **Article 75** deals with the appointment, tenure, responsibility, qualification, oath, and salaries of the ministers.
 
• **Size of Council of Ministers**: According to the **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003**, the total number of ministers, including the **Prime Minister**, in the **Central Council of Ministers** shall not exceed **15%** of the total strength of the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• **Collective Responsibility**: Under **Article 75(3)**, the **Council of Ministers** is **collectively responsible** to the **Lok Sabha** (the **Lower House** of **Parliament**). This means that all ministers own joint responsibility to the **Lok Sabha** for all their acts of omission and commission.
 
• **Cabinet vs. Council of Ministers**: The **Council of Ministers** is a wider body consisting of **60 to 80 ministers**, whereas the **Cabinet** is a smaller, more powerful core group consisting of about **15 to 20 ministers**. The term "Cabinet" was inserted into **Article 352** of the **Constitution** by the **44th Amendment Act, 1978**.
 
• **Appointment**: The **Prime Minister** is appointed by the **President**, and other ministers are appointed by the **President** on the recommendation of the **Prime Minister**. A person who is not a member of either **House of Parliament** can be appointed as a minister for a maximum period of **6 months**, within which they must get elected to either house.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Individual Responsibility**: **Article 75** also contains the principle of **individual responsibility**, stating that the ministers hold office during the **pleasure of the President**.
 
• **Council Hierarchy**: While the **Constitution** does not classify the ministers into different ranks, this three-tier classification is based on **British parliamentary conventions** and has been followed in **India** since independence.
 
• **Parliamentary Secretaries**: Occasionally, a fourth category known as **Parliamentary Secretaries** is also appointed. They are senior members of the **ruling party** who assist the ministers in their **parliamentary duties** but are not technically part of the **Council of Ministers**.

questions.question: Along a circular running track, P can complete 5 rounds in 40 minutes. Time taken by R to complete 7 rounds is equal to time taken by P to complete 6 rounds. If they start running in the same direction from two different ends of a diameter, then they will meet for the first time after ____ minutes.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for P per round = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 min.

Time for R per round = (6 × 8) ÷ 7 = 48/7 min.

In same direction, Relative Speed = |1/8 − 7/48| = 1/48 rounds/min.

Initial gap = 1/2 round (diameter ends).

Time to meet = (1/2) ÷ (1/48) = 24 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rounds by P = 5 in 40 min.

Relation: Time for 7 rounds of R = Time for 6 rounds of P.

Start position: Opposite ends of diameter (1/2 track apart).

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

Time of Meeting = Initial Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 
• P R 
 Initial Gap = 1/2 Round Same Direction Motion 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let track length = L

⇒ Speed of P (SP) = (5 × L) ÷ 40 = L/8 per min

⇒ Time for 6 rounds of P = 6 × (L ÷ SP) = 6 × 8 = 48 min

⇒ Speed of R (SR) = (7 × L) ÷ 48 = 7L/48 per min

⇒ Initial separation distance = L/2 (Diameter ends)

⇒ Relative Speed = SR − SP = 7L/48 − L/8

⇒ Relative Speed = 7L/48 − 6L/48 = L/48 per min

⇒ Meeting Time = (L/2) ÷ (L/48)

⇒ Meeting Time = (1/2) × 48 = 24 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 24 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting in Opposite Direction

When two people run in opposite directions, the relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Number of Meeting Points

If speeds are in ratio a:b (simplest form), they meet at (a−b) points in the same direction and (a+b) points in opposite directions.

Time for Subsequent Meetings

After the first meeting, each subsequent meeting occurs after a time interval of (Total Distance) ÷ (Relative Speed).

Recognize roots: √³2744 = 14 and √⁴256 = 4.

Substitute into expression: (14 ÷ 4) × (2 ÷ 42) × 72

Reduce ratios: (7 ÷ 2) × (1 ÷ 21) × 72

Combine: (7 ÷ 21) × (72 ÷ 2) = (1 ÷ 3) × 36 = 12

**∴ Answer = 12**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Expression: (√³2744 ÷ √⁴256) × (2 ÷ 42) × 72

**Formula used:**

Root property: √ⁿxⁿ = x

BODMAS rule: Simplify terms within brackets and roots first, then perform multiplication.

 
• 
• Term 1 Term 2 Term 3 14 / 4 2 / 42 72 Calculation: 3.5 × (1/21) × 72 = 12 

**Calculations:**

Step 1: Simplify individual roots

⇒ √³2744 = √³(14 × 14 × 14) = 14

⇒ √⁴256 = √⁴(4 × 4 × 4 × 4) = 4

Step 2: Substitute and simplify fractions

⇒ (14 ÷ 4) × (2 ÷ 42) × 72

⇒ 3.5 × (1 ÷ 21) × 72

Step 3: Solve the multiplication

⇒ (3.5 ÷ 21) × 72

⇒ (1 ÷ 6) × 72

⇒ 72 ÷ 6 = 12

Always prioritize Roots/Exponents (Orders) and Brackets before performing Multiplication and Division from left to right.

questions.question: Which provision of the Indian Council Act of 1909 was most criticised for weakening the unity of the Indian nationalist movement?

options.text: Inclusion of Indians in the Governor-General’s Council
Introduction of executive councils in presidencies

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Creation of separate electorates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Council Act of 1909**, also famously known as the **Morley-Minto Reforms**, introduced the highly controversial system of **separate electorates** for **Muslims**. Under this provision, **Muslim representatives** were to be elected exclusively by **Muslim voters**.
 
• This move was criticized by the **Indian National Congress** and other nationalist leaders as it was perceived as a clear application of the **"Divide and Rule" policy**. By institutionalizing **communalism** in Indian politics, the **British Government** aimed to create a rift between **Hindus** and **Muslims**, thereby weakening the **Nationalist Movement**.
 
• The Act was named after **Lord Morley**, the then **Secretary of State for India**, and **Lord Minto**, the **Viceroy of India**. Due to his role in introducing communal representation, **Lord Minto** is often referred to as the **"Father of Communal Electorate"**.
 
• The **Creation of separate electorates** is the correct answer because it directly targeted the unity of the Indian people by categorizing political interests based on religion, which eventually laid the groundwork for the **Partition of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Expansion of Legislative Councils:** The Act increased the size of the **Legislative Councils** at both the **Central** and **Provincial** levels. The number of members in the **Central Legislative Council** was raised from **16 to 60**. However, an **official majority** was retained at the **Centre**, while **non-official majorities** were allowed in the **Provincial Councils**.
 
• **Inclusion of Indians in Executive Councils:** For the first time, the Act provided for the association of Indians with the **Executive Councils** of the **Viceroy** and **Governors**. **Satyendra Prasad Sinha** became the first Indian to join the **Viceroy’s Executive Council** as the **Law Member**.
 
• **Enhanced Deliberative Powers:** The **Legislative Councils** were given the power to discuss the **Budget** and move **resolutions**. Members were also allowed to ask **supplementary questions**, although the executive still held the final authority and could reject resolutions without providing detailed reasons.
 
• **Background of the Act:** The reforms were enacted in the backdrop of the **1905 Partition of Bengal** and the formation of the **All India Muslim League** in **1906**. The **Simla Deputation**, led by **Aga Khan** in **1906**, had specifically met **Lord Minto** to demand separate representation for Muslims to safeguard their political rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Morley-Minto Reforms** did not aim at establishing a **parliamentary system** in India; rather, they were intended to involve some Indians in the administration to placate the **Moderate** faction of the **Congress** while isolating the **Extremists**.
 
• The system of **communal representation** introduced in **1909** was further extended to **Sikhs**, **Indian Christians**, **Anglo-Indians**, and **Europeans** in the **Government of India Act 1919** (**Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**).
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** later stated that "The **Morley-Minto Reforms** have been our undoing," emphasizing how the **Creation of separate electorates** sowed the seeds of **communal disharmony** that plagued the independence struggle for decades.
 
• Despite the increase in the number of members, the **electorate** remained very limited, based on **property qualifications**, **education**, or **status**, meaning only a tiny fraction of the Indian population had the **Right to Vote**.

questions.question: Which of the following reflects the structural adjustment in India’s monetary policy after the 1991 economic reforms?

options.text: Controlled lending rates for agriculture and MSMEs
Market-determined interest rates with reduced RBI intervention
Elimination of open market operations as a regulatory tool
Expansion of currency supply through deficit financing

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Market-determined interest rates with reduced RBI intervention**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• One of the most significant structural adjustments in India’s monetary policy following the **1991 Economic Reforms** was the shift from an **administered interest rate regime** to a **market-determined interest rate system**. Prior to **1991**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** strictly controlled interest rates for both deposits and loans.
 
• The **Narasimham Committee (1991)** on the Financial System recommended that interest rates should be allowed to be determined by **market forces** (demand and supply) to improve the efficiency of the banking sector and the allocation of capital. ***Hence, the statement regarding market-determined rates is correct.***
 
• Post-reforms, the **RBI** gradually deregulated lending and deposit rates. By **October 1994**, the **RBI** abolished the minimum lending rate and allowed commercial banks to determine their own **Prime Lending Rates (PLR)**.
 
• This shift allowed the **RBI** to move away from direct controls and instead use **indirect instruments** of monetary policy, such as the **Repo Rate**, **Reverse Repo Rate**, and **Open Market Operations (OMO)**, to manage liquidity and inflation in the **Indian economy**.
 
• The structural adjustment also involved a significant reduction in the **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** and **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**. The **SLR**, which was as high as **38.5%** in **1991**, was gradually brought down to increase the availability of funds for the private sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1991 Economic Crisis:** India faced a severe **Balance of Payments (BoP)** crisis in **1991**, with **forex reserves** dropping to a level barely enough to cover two weeks of imports. This led to the **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)** reforms under the leadership of **Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao** and **Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• **Monetary Policy Tools:**
 
 
• **Open Market Operations (OMO):** Post-1991, **OMOs** became a vital regulatory tool. The **RBI** buys or sells **Government Securities (G-Secs)** to regulate the money supply. Statement 3 is incorrect because **OMOs** were strengthened, not eliminated.
 
• **Deficit Financing:** Before the reforms, the government relied heavily on **automatic monetization** of the **fiscal deficit** through **Ad-hoc Treasury Bills**. This was phased out by **1997** and eventually replaced by the **Ways and Means Advances (WMA)** system. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect as the goal was to curtail deficit financing.***
 
 
 
• **Priority Sector Lending (PSL):** While the government still mandates **40%** of **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** to the **Priority Sector** (including **Agriculture** and **MSMEs**), the overall structural trend moved away from general "controlled rates" toward market alignment, even within these sectors. ***Hence, statement 1 is partially true in practice but does not represent the "structural adjustment" of the reform era.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF):** Introduced in **June 2000** following the **Narasimham Committee II (1998)** recommendations, **LAF** allowed banks to manage their day-to-day liquidity mismatches through **repo** and **reverse repo** auctions.
 
• **MCLR and EBLR:** To ensure better transmission of **monetary policy**, the **RBI** transitioned from the **Base Rate** system to the **Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate (MCLR)** in **2016**, and subsequently to **External Benchmark Lending Rates (EBLR)** in **2019** for retail and **MSME** loans.
 
• **FRBM Act (2003):** The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act** was enacted to institutionalize fiscal discipline and reduce the **fiscal deficit**, further separating **monetary policy** from the government’s **fiscal deficit** requirements.

questions.question: Who were the "Samantas" in the post-Gupta period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Feudal lords**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Samanta** refers to big landlords or **warrior chiefs** in different regions of the Indian subcontinent during the **post-Gupta period** (specifically between the **6th and 12th centuries CE**). ***Hence, the option identifying them as Feudal lords is correct.***
 
• These individuals were expected to bring **gifts** or **tributes** for their kings or overlords and provide them with **military support** during times of war.
 
• As **Samantas** gained power and wealth, they often declared themselves to be **Mahasamanta** or **Mahamandaleshvara** (the great lord of a circle or region), indicating an increase in their social and political status.
 
• The **Samanta system** led to the **decentralization** of political power, where the central monarch's authority became dependent on the loyalty of these subordinate **feudal lords**.
 
• If a **Samanta** became powerful enough, he could assert **independence** from his overlord. A famous example is **Dantidurga**, a **Rashtrakuta** chief who overthrew his **Chalikya** overlord in the **mid-8th century**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Farmers:** In the ancient and medieval periods, farmers were known as **Krishakas** or **Halikas**. While they provided the **revenue** that supported the Samantas, they did not hold administrative or military titles. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Religious heads:** Religious leaders or priests (**Brahmins**) often received **land grants** known as **Agrahara** or **Brahmadeya**. While they managed land, their primary identity was spiritual and ritualistic rather than the military-administrative role associated with Samantas. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Architects:** Professional builders and designers in ancient India were referred to as **Shilpis** or **Sutradharas**. They were responsible for the **temple architecture** of the era, such as the **Khajuraho** or **Chola** temples, but held no feudal authority. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Origin of the System:** The practice of granting land to officers in lieu of **cash salaries** began during the **Gupta Empire** and became a dominant feature under King **Harshavardhana** in the **7th Century CE**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The rise of the Samantas led to a **manorial economy** where the **peasantry** was often tied to the land, and **local self-sufficiency** became more prominent than long-distance trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Administrative Structure:** The **Samantas** were responsible for maintaining **law and order** within their territories and **collecting taxes**, a portion of which was sent to the king.
 
• **Military Obligation:** One of the primary duties of a **Samanta** was to maintain a specific number of **infantry** and **cavalry** units to be placed at the king's disposal whenever required.
 
• **Geographical Spread:** This system was prevalent across **North India** under the **Pratiharas** and **Palas**, and in **South India** under the **Rashtrakutas** and **Pallavas**.
 
• **Social Hierarchy:** The Samanta occupied a middle position in the **social hierarchy**, acting as a bridge between the **monarch** and the **common people** (peasants and artisans).
 
• **End of the System:** The **Samanta system** began to decline with the advent of the **Delhi Sultanate**, which introduced a more centralized **Iqta system** of administration.

questions.question: How often does India submit its Biennial Update Reports (BURs) to the UNFCCC?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Every two years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Biennial Update Reports (BURs)** are specialized reports submitted by **Non-Annex I** parties (developing countries like **India**) to the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**.
 
• According to the guidelines established during the **Conference of Parties (COP 16)** in **Cancun (2010)** and **COP 17** in **Durban (2011)**, these reports must be submitted **every two years**.
 
• The primary objective of the **BUR** is to provide an update on the information presented in the **National Communications (NATCOM)**, specifically focusing on **national greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories**, **mitigation actions** and their effects, and the **support needed and received**.
 
• **India** submitted its **First BUR** to the **UNFCCC** in **January 2016**, the **Second BUR** in **December 2018**, and the **Third BUR** in **February 2021**.
 
• The **Third BUR** highlighted that **India** has successfully reduced the **emission intensity** of its **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** by **24%** between **2005** and **2016**, showcasing significant progress toward its **Paris Agreement** goals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UNFCCC (United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change):**

 
 
• It was adopted in **1992** at the **Rio Earth Summit** and entered into force on **March 21, 1994**.
 
• Its ultimate objective is to stabilize **greenhouse gas concentrations** in the atmosphere at a level that prevents dangerous human interference with the climate system.
 
• It categorizes countries into **Annex I** (developed nations), **Annex II** (developed nations providing financial support), and **Non-Annex I** (mostly developing nations).
 
 
 
• **National Communications (NATCOM):**
 
 
• These are comprehensive reports that **India** is required to submit periodically. **India** submitted **NATCOM-1** in **2004**, **NATCOM-2** in **2012**, and **NATCOM-3** in **2023**.
 
• Unlike **BURs** which occur **every two years**, **NATCOMs** have a longer and more flexible reporting cycle depending on **COP** decisions.
 
 
 
• **Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF):**
 
 
• Under the **Paris Agreement** (signed in **2015**), the reporting system is transitioning from **BURs** to **Biennial Transparency Reports (BTRs)**.
 
• The **first BTR** for all parties is mandated to be submitted by **December 31, 2024**. This will provide a more rigorous and uniform tracking mechanism for **Climate Action** globally.
 
 
 
• **India’s GHG Inventory Sectors:**
 
 
• **India** reports emissions from five major sectors: **Energy**, **Industrial Processes and Product Use (IPPU)**, **Agriculture**, **Waste**, and **Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry (LULUCF)**.
 
• The **Energy sector** remains the largest contributor to emissions in **India**, accounting for approximately **75%** of total emissions (excluding **LULUCF**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Institutional Arrangement:** In **India**, the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** is the nodal agency responsible for preparing and submitting these reports to the **UNFCCC**.
 
• **Technical Analysis:** Once a **BUR** is submitted, it undergoes a **Technical Analysis** by a team of international experts as part of the **International Consultation and Analysis (ICA)** process.
 
• **Yearly Submissions:** While the question asks about **BURs** (which are **every two years**), developed countries (**Annex I**) are required to submit their **GHG inventories** **every year**.
 
• **Global Context:** The **BUR** helps in the **Global Stocktake** process, which assesses the collective progress of the world toward achieving the long-term goals of the **Paris Agreement**.

questions.question: Which nutrient is primarily responsible for building and repairing tissues in the human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Proteins** are known as the **building blocks** of the human body. Their primary **function** is the **growth**, **maintenance**, and **repair** of all **body tissues**, including **muscles**, **organs**, **skin**, and **hair**.
 
• Chemically, proteins are **macromolecules** composed of smaller units called **amino acids**. There are **20** different amino acids that combine in various sequences to form different proteins. Unlike carbohydrates and fats, proteins contain **nitrogen** in addition to **carbon**, **hydrogen**, and **oxygen**.
 
• Proteins act as **enzymes**, which are **biological catalysts** that speed up chemical reactions in the body. For **example**, digestive enzymes like **pepsin** and **trypsin** are essential for breaking down food.
 
• They also serve as **hormones**, such as **insulin**, which regulates **blood sugar levels**. Furthermore, **antibodies** are specialized proteins that are critical to the **immune system** for defending the body against **viruses** and **bacteria**.
 
• When the body lacks sufficient **carbohydrates** or **fats**, it can break down proteins to provide **energy**, yielding approximately **4 kcal** per **1 gram** of protein.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Carbohydrates:**

 
 
• The primary **function** of carbohydrates is to provide immediate **energy** to the body. They are broken down into **glucose**, which is the preferred **fuel** for the **brain** and **muscles**.
 
• Sources include **cereals**, **fruits**, and **vegetables**. They provide **4 kcal** per **gram**.
 
 
 
• **Fats:**
 
 
• Fats serve as a **concentrated source of energy**, providing **9 kcal** per **gram**, which is more than double the energy provided by proteins or carbs.
 
• They are essential for the **absorption** of **fat-soluble vitamins** like **Vitamin A**, **D**, **E**, and **K**. They also provide **insulation** and protect internal **organs**.
 
 
 
• **Vitamins:**
 
 
• Vitamins are **micronutrients** required in **small quantities** for various **metabolic** processes. They do not provide energy but are crucial for **bone health**, **vision**, and **blood clotting**.
 
• Examples include **Vitamin C** (for **immunity**) and **Vitamin D** (for **calcium absorption**).
 
 
 
• **Minerals:**
 
 
• Inorganic elements like **Calcium**, **Iron**, and **Potassium** are necessary for **bone density**, **oxygen transport** in the **blood** (via **hemoglobin**), and **nerve signaling**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Essential Amino Acids:** Out of the **20** amino acids, **9** are considered **essential** because the human body cannot **synthesize** them; they must be obtained through **diet**.
 
• **Dietary Requirements:** According to **health guidelines**, the **Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA)** for an **adult** is approximately **0.8 grams** of protein per **kilogram** of **body weight**. This requirement increases for **infants**, **pregnant women**, and **athletes**.
 
• **Deficiency Diseases:** Severe **protein deficiency** leads to conditions like **Kwashiorkor** (characterized by **edema** and a **swollen abdomen**) and **Marasmus** (characterized by **stunted growth** and **tissue wasting**), commonly seen in **children** in **developing countries**.
 
• **Structural Proteins:** **Collagen** is the most abundant protein in the human body, providing **structure** to **connective tissues**, while **Keratin** is the primary component of **nails** and **hair**.

⇒ 6² = a × (4a)

Mean Proportional

In the proportion a : b :: c : d, d is the fourth proportional and is given by d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Continued Proportion

Quantities a, b, c, d... are in continued proportion if a/b = b/c = c/d and so on.

questions.question: Which of the following reflects the Gandhian ideals incorporated as Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution of India?

options.text: Raising the standard of living and public health
Promoting cottage industries in rural areas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Promoting cottage industries in rural areas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** are enumerated in **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution, spanning from **Article 36 to 51**. These principles are classified into **Socialistic**, **Gandhian**, and **Liberal-Intellectual** categories based on their ideology.
 
• **Article 43** of the Constitution directs the State to endeavor to promote **cottage industries** on an individual or co-operative basis in **rural areas**. This reflects **Mahatma Gandhi’s** vision of self-sufficient village economies and rural upliftment. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Raising the standard of living and **public health** is mentioned under **Article 47**. While it aligns with the overall welfare state, it is primarily categorized as a **Socialistic Principle** rather than a specific Gandhian ideal in the classification of the Constitution. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Securing **suitable employment** for all is part of the "Right to Work" under **Article 41**. This directive is a **Socialistic Principle** aimed at ensuring economic security for citizens. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Safeguarding **children** against **exploitation** and providing them with opportunities for healthy development is covered under **Article 39(f)**. This is classified as a **Socialistic Principle** added or emphasized to ensure social justice. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gandhian Principles in DPSP:** These principles are based on the ideology of **Mahatma Gandhi** and represent the program of reconstruction enunciated by him during the **National Movement**.

 
 
• **Article 40:** To organize **village panchayats** and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.
 
• **Article 43B:** To promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of **co-operative societies** (Added by the **97th Amendment Act, 2011**).
 
• **Article 46:** To promote the educational and economic interests of **Scheduled Castes (SCs)**, **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**, and other weaker sections of the society and to protect them from social injustice and all forms of **exploitation**.
 
• **Article 47:** To prohibit the consumption of **intoxicating drinks** and drugs that are injurious to health.
 
• **Article 48:** To prohibit the **slaughter of cows**, calves, and other milch and draught cattle and to improve their breeds.
 
 
 
• **Socialistic Principles:** These aim at establishing **social and economic justice** and paving the way for a welfare state. Examples include **Article 38** (promoting social order), **Article 39** (equitable distribution of resources), and **Article 42** (humane conditions of work and **maternity relief**).
 
• **Liberal-Intellectual Principles:** These reflect the ideology of **liberalism**. Examples include **Article 44** (**Uniform Civil Code**), **Article 50** (Separation of judiciary from executive), and **Article 51** (Promotion of **international peace** and security).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **DPSP** are borrowed from the **Irish Constitution** of **1937**, which had copied them from the **Spanish Constitution**.
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, **DPSPs** are **non-justiciable** in nature, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation (as per **Article 37**). However, they are fundamental in the governance of the **country**.
 
• The **Sapru Committee** in **1945** suggested two categories of individual rights: one being justiciable (Fundamental Rights) and the other being non-justiciable (Directive Principles).
 
• In the **Minerva Mills Case (1980)**, the **Supreme Court** held that the **Indian Constitution** is founded on the bedrock of the balance between **Fundamental Rights** and the **Directive Principles**.

questions.question: ​On which river in India is the National Waterway 57 (NW-57) developed?

The correct answer is __**Kopili River**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Waterway 57 (NW-57)** is developed on the **Kopili River**, located in the state of **Assam**. **Hence, the option Kopili River is correct.**
 
• The stretch of **NW-57** spans a length of approximately **48 kilometers**, extending from the **confluence of the Kopili River with the Brahmaputra River** to the **Teliagaon Railway Bridge**.
 
• This waterway was officially designated under the **National Waterways Act, 2016**, which aimed to promote inland water transport as a fuel-efficient and cost-effective mode of logistics in **India**.
 
• The **Kopili River** is a significant **south-bank tributary** of the **Brahmaputra River**, flowing through the states of **Meghalaya** and **Assam**.
 
• The development of **NW-57** is managed by the **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI)**, which is the statutory authority in charge of the waterways in the **country**.

questions.question: Which of the following cabinet committees is NOT headed by the Prime Minister?

options.text: Cabinet committee on employment and skill development
Cabinet committee on investment and growth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cabinet committee on parliamentary affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs** is the only major cabinet committee that is **NOT** headed by the **Prime Minister**; instead, it is typically chaired by the **Union Home Minister**.
 
• The primary function of this committee is to look after the progress of government business in the **Parliament of India** and ensure smooth coordination between the two houses, **Lok Sabha** and **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The **Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)** is chaired by the **Prime Minister**. It is responsible for reviewing economic trends and evolving an integrated strategy for policies like **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** and various developmental projects.
 
• The **Cabinet Committee on Investment and Growth** was newly constituted in **June 2019** and is headed by the **Prime Minister** to identify key projects for implementation on a time-bound basis.
 
• The **Cabinet Committee on Employment and Skill Development**, also created in **2019**, is headed by the **Prime Minister** and focuses on providing a direction to various initiatives for **skill development** and increasing employability in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Cabinet Committees:** These are **extra-constitutional** bodies, meaning they are not mentioned in the **Constitution of India**. They are established under the **Government of India Transaction of Business Rules, 1961**.
 
• **Types:** There are two types of committees: **Standing Committees**, which are of a permanent nature, and **Ad-hoc Committees**, which are temporary and formed for specific tasks.
 
• **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet:** This committee is headed by the **Prime Minister** and includes the **Home Minister**. It decides on all higher-level appointments in the **Central Secretariat**, **Public Sector Undertakings**, and **Banks**.
 
• **Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS):** Chaired by the **Prime Minister**, it deals with issues of national security, defense expenditure, and external affairs that impact **India's** security.
 
• **Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs:** This is often described as a **"Super-Cabinet"** because it deals with all policy matters pertaining to domestic and foreign affairs. It is chaired by the **Prime Minister**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Membership:** While the number of members in these committees can vary from **3 to 8**, they usually include **Cabinet Ministers**. Non-cabinet ministers can sometimes be invited as special invitees.
 
• **Cabinet Committee on Accommodation:** Like the Parliamentary Affairs committee, this committee is also usually headed by the **Union Home Minister**. It deals with the allotment of government accommodation to **Members of Parliament** and other officials.
 
• **Role in Governance:** These committees serve as an organizational device to reduce the enormous workload of the **Cabinet** and facilitate **in-depth examination** of policy issues and effective coordination.
 
• **Evolution:** The number and nomenclature of these committees change with the change in **Government**. For instance, in **2019**, the **NDA government** re-constituted **8** committees, emphasizing **Investment** and **Employment**.

Since it is situated in **North India** and not in **Maharashtra**, it is not part of the Daulatabad complex. ***Hence, statement 1 is the correct answer.***
 
• **Chand Minar**: Also known as the **Tower of the Moon**, this massive tower is located within the **Daulatabad Fort** in **Maharashtra**. questions.question: Which ratio is the largest among 5 : 12, 14 : 31, 8 : 33 and 17 : 39?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert ratios to approximate decimals for instant comparison:

5 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.417

14 ÷ 31 ≈ 0.452

8 ÷ 33 ≈ 0.242

17 ÷ 39 ≈ 0.436

Comparing decimals: 0.452 > 0.436 > 0.417 > 0.242

**∴ Answer = 14 : 31**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Ratios to compare: 5 : 12, 14 : 31, 8 : 33, and 17 : 39

**Formula used:**

Ratio a : b can be written as fraction a/b. To compare two fractions a/b and c/d, check if a × d > b × c.

 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 0.2 0.3 0.4 0.5 8:33 5:12 17:39 14:31 (Largest) Comparison on Decimal Scale 

**Calculations:**

Compare 14/31 with 5/12:

⇒ 14 × 12 = 168 and 31 × 5 = 155. Since 168 > 155, 14 : 31 > 5 : 12.

Compare 14/31 with 17/39:

⇒ 14 × 39 = 546 and 31 × 17 = 527. Since 546 > 527, 14 : 31 > 17 : 39.

Compare 14/31 with 8/33:

⇒ 14 × 33 = 462 and 31 × 8 = 248. Since 462 > 248, 14 : 31 > 8 : 33.

Comparing all values, 14 : 31 is the largest ratio.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 : 31 (Option 2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cross-Multiplication Rule

For any two ratios a/b and c/d, if (a × d) > (b × c), then a/b > c/d. This is the most accurate method to compare fractions without decimals.

Percentage Conversion Method

Convert ratios to percentages by multiplying by 100. For example, 5 : 12 ≈ 41.67% and 14 : 31 ≈ 45.16%.

Common Denominator Method

Find the LCM of all denominators and convert all fractions to have this common denominator. The fraction with the largest numerator will be the largest ratio.

questions.question: According to the Government of India, flash floods in July 2023 in which state severely disrupted the functioning of several power stations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **July 2023**, the state of **Himachal Pradesh** witnessed unprecedented rainfall and cloudbursts, leading to catastrophic **flash floods** and landslides that severely crippled the power generation infrastructure. Hence, the statement that flash floods in Himachal Pradesh disrupted power stations in July 2023 is **correct**.
 
• The heavy rains caused a massive increase in the **silt content** (turbidity) of the **Satluj** and **Beas** rivers, forcing the immediate shutdown of several major **Hydroelectric Projects (HEPs)** to prevent damage to the turbine blades.
 
• Key power stations affected included the **1,500 MW Nathpa Jhakri** Hydro Power Station, which is India’s largest underground hydroelectric project, and the **412 MW Rampur** Hydro Power Station.
 
• The **silt levels** in the rivers reportedly crossed **10,000 parts per million (ppm)**, far exceeding the permissible limit of **2,000 to 3,000 ppm** required for safe operation.
 
• This disruption led to a significant shortfall in the **Northern Grid**, affecting the power supply to several states including **Punjab**, **Haryana**, and **Delhi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geography and Vulnerability:** **Himachal Pradesh** is a mountainous state in **North India** characterized by steep slopes and fragile ecosystems. In **2023**, the combination of the **Southwest Monsoon** and a **Western Disturbance** led to extreme precipitation events in districts like **Kullu**, **Mandi**, and **Shimla**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The state government estimated the total economic loss due to the floods at over **10,000 crore rupees**, involving the destruction of over **40 bridges**, several **National Highways (NH-3 and NH-5)**, and hundreds of small water supply schemes.
 
• **SJVN Limited:** The **Satluj Jal Vidyut Nigam (SJVN)**, a **Mini Ratna** public sector undertaking, manages the **Nathpa Jhakri** and **Rampur** projects. They had to halt operations for several days during the **July 7–11, 2023** peak flood period.
 
• **Comparison with Other States:** While **Sikkim** faced a major glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) affecting the **Teesta III** dam, that event occurred in **October 2023**, not July. **Uttarakhand** and **Arunachal Pradesh** also have high hydropower potential but did not report power station shutdowns of this specific scale during the **July 2023** window.
 
• **Hydropower Significance:** **Himachal Pradesh** is often referred to as the **"Power State"** of India, with an estimated hydropower potential of about **27,436 MW**, accounting for approximately **25%** of the national potential.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Role of Turbidity:** High **silt** or **turbidity** acts like sandpaper on the metallic parts of the turbines. If the projects are not shut down, the **abrasive action** of quartz and other minerals in the silt can lead to **erosion** of the runners and guide vanes, requiring expensive and time-consuming repairs.
 
• **Disaster Management:** The **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** and the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** were deployed to rescue thousands of tourists and locals stranded in the **Lahaul-Spiti** and **Kullu** valleys during this period.
 
• **Climate Change:** Experts suggest that the increasing frequency of such **flash floods** in the **Himalayas** is a direct consequence of **climate change** and **global warming**, leading to unpredictable rainfall patterns in high-altitude regions.

questions.question: Line AB is parallel to line CD. A transversal PQ intersects AB at M and CD at N. If angle PMB = (5x)º, angle BMN = (3x + 2y)º and angle DNQ = (x + 3y)º then find the value of angle BMN.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Linear pair at M: 5x + (3x + 2y) = 180 ⇒ 8x + 2y = 180 ⇒ 4x + y = 90

Since AB || CD, ∠PMB = corresponding ∠MND = 5x

Linear pair at N: ∠MND + ∠DNQ = 5x + (x + 3y) = 180 ⇒ 6x + 3y = 180 ⇒ 2x + y = 60

Solving: (4x + y) − (2x + y) = 90 − 60 ⇒ 2x = 30 ⇒ x = 15

Substituting x = 15 in 2x + y = 60 gives y = 30

∠BMN = 3(15) + 2(30) = 45 + 60 = 105°

**∴ Answer = 105°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Line AB || Line CD with transversal PQ intersecting at M and N.

∠PMB = 5x°, ∠BMN = (3x + 2y)°, and ∠DNQ = (x + 3y)°

**Formula used:**

1. Sum of angles in a linear pair = 180°

2. Corresponding angles of parallel lines are equal.

 
• 
• 
• A B C D P Q M N 5x 3x + 2y x + 3y AB || CD 

**Calculations:**

∠PMB and ∠BMN form a linear pair on transversal PQ at intersection M.

⇒ ∠PMB + ∠BMN = 180°

⇒ 5x + 3x + 2y = 180 ⇒ 8x + 2y = 180 ⇒ 4x + y = 90 --- (Eq. 1)

Since AB || CD, the corresponding angles ∠PMB and ∠MND are equal.

⇒ ∠MND = ∠PMB = 5x

∠MND and ∠DNQ form a linear pair on transversal PQ at intersection N.

⇒ ∠MND + ∠DNQ = 180°

⇒ 5x + x + 3y = 180 ⇒ 6x + 3y = 180 ⇒ 2x + y = 60 --- (Eq. 2)

Subtracting (Eq. 2) from (Eq. 1):

⇒ (4x + y) − (2x + y) = 90 − 60 ⇒ 2x = 30 ⇒ x = 15

Putting x = 15 in (Eq. 2):

⇒ 2(15) + y = 60 ⇒ 30 + y = 60 ⇒ y = 30

Now, finding the value of ∠BMN:

⇒ ∠BMN = 3x + 2y = 3(15) + 2(30) = 45 + 60 = 105°

**∴ The correct answer is 105°, which is option (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Pair of Angles

When two angles are adjacent and their non-common sides form a straight line, they are supplementary, i.e., Sum = 180°.

Parallel Lines and Transversal

When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal, alternate interior angles are equal, and consecutive interior angles are supplementary (sum = 180°).

Vertically Opposite Angles

When two lines intersect, the angles opposite to each other at the vertex are always equal.

questions.question: During PM Narendra Modi’s **State Visit to Bhutan (11–12 Nov 2025)**, which **hydroelectric project** was jointly inaugurated?

questions.question: In 2025, which city topped the National Air Quality Index released for major Indian cities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shillong**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Air Quality Index (NAQI)** released for the year **2025** indicates that **Shillong**, the capital of **Meghalaya**, has emerged as the city with the cleanest air among major Indian urban centers.
 
• The report, typically compiled by the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**, monitors the air quality across various states and union territories using a **real-time monitoring system**.
 
• **Shillong** consistently records an **AQI (Air Quality Index)** value within the **'Good'** category (0-50), primarily due to its **geographical elevation**, extensive **forest cover**, and relatively lower **industrial density** compared to metropolitan hubs.

questions.question: Side PQ of a cyclic quadrilateral PQRS is produced to the point T. Ifangle RQT = 58º , then the measure of angle PSR is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the exterior angle is always equal to the interior opposite angle.

Side PQ is produced to point T, so the exterior angle at vertex Q is angle RQT.

The interior opposite angle to vertex Q is angle PSR.

Logic: angle PSR = angle RQT = 58°

**∴ Answer = 58°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral. Side PQ is produced to point T. Exterior angle RQT = 58°.

**Formula used:**

Sum of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral = 180°

Linear pair sum = 180° (Angles on a straight line)

 
 
• P Q R S T 58° ? 
 
 

**Calculations:**

Since PQT is a straight line, angle PQR + angle RQT = 180°

⇒ angle PQR + 58° = 180°

⇒ angle PQR = 180° − 58° = 122°

In cyclic quadrilateral PQRS, the sum of opposite angles is 180°:

⇒ angle PSR + angle PQR = 180°

⇒ angle PSR + 122° = 180°

⇒ angle PSR = 180° − 122° = 58°

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Quadrilateral Opposite Angles

The sum of either pair of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°.

Exterior Angle Property

The exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is equal to the interior opposite angle.

Brahmagupta's Formula

Area of a cyclic quadrilateral = √((s−a)(s−b)(s−c)(s−d)), where s is the semi-perimeter (a+b+c+d)/2.

Ptolemy's Theorem

For a cyclic quadrilateral, the product of the diagonals is equal to the sum of the products of the opposite sides: d₁ × d₂ = (a × c) + (b × d).

questions.question: Which ions help chlorophyll to absorb light?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorophyll** is the green pigment found in the **chloroplasts** of plants, algae, and cyanobacteria, which is essential for the process of **photosynthesis**.
 
• The central component of the **chlorophyll** molecule is a **Magnesium (Mg)** ion, which is held within a large heterocyclic ring known as a **porphyrin** (or chlorin) ring. ***Hence, the statement regarding Mg is correct.***
 
• **Magnesium** acts as the coordination center for the **tetrapyrrole** ring; its presence is vital because it helps in the **absorption of light energy**, specifically in the **blue** and **red** regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.
 
• Without the **Mg** ion, the pigment would be called **pheophytin**, which lacks the efficiency to capture solar energy for driving the **light-dependent reactions** of photosynthesis.
 
• In plants, **Magnesium** deficiency often leads to a condition called **chlorosis**, where the leaves turn **yellow** due to the breakdown of chlorophyll, significantly reducing the plant's ability to produce food.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Calcium (Ca)**: This element is primarily used by plants for **cell wall** synthesis and maintaining the structural integrity of **membranes**. It exists as **calcium pectate** in the middle lamella. While it is a crucial **macronutrient**, it does not play a direct role as a central ion in light absorption within chlorophyll. ***Hence, the statement regarding Ca is incorrect.***
 
• **Sodium (Na)**: Although it is essential for certain **C4 plants** and **CAM plants** to help in the regeneration of **phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP)**, it is not a part of the chlorophyll structure. In most **C3 plants**, it is not considered an essential nutrient for light absorption. ***Hence, the statement regarding Na is incorrect.***
 
• **Carbon (C)**: Carbon is the fundamental building block of all **organic molecules**, including the skeleton of chlorophyll. However, in the context of this question, **Carbon** is an element forming the structure rather than an "ion" that specifically aids the absorption of light in the coordination center. ***Hence, the statement regarding C is incorrect.***
 
• The primary types of chlorophyll found in terrestrial plants are **Chlorophyll a** and **Chlorophyll b**. **Chlorophyll a** is the primary electron donor in the **reaction center**, while **Chlorophyll b** acts as an **accessory pigment** to broaden the spectrum of light absorbed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Structural Composition**: The **porphyrin ring** of chlorophyll is chemically similar to the **heme** group in **hemoglobin** found in human blood, with the primary difference being that chlorophyll contains **Magnesium** at its center, whereas hemoglobin contains **Iron (Fe)**.
 
• **Functionality**: The **Mg++** ion is coordinated to four **nitrogen** atoms within the ring. This specific electronic configuration allows the molecule to enter an **excited state** when struck by **photons**, initiating the **electron transport chain**.
 
• **Discovery**: The chemical structure of chlorophyll was elucidated by **Richard Willstätter** and **Arthur Stoll** in **1913**, a feat for which Willstätter was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Chemistry** in **1915**.
 
• **Applications**: Understanding the role of **Magnesium** in chlorophyll is vital for **agriculture**. Farmers use **Epsom salts** (magnesium sulfate) to treat **Magnesium** deficiency in soil to boost crop yields and ensure healthy green foliage.

questions.question: In 2025, which United Nations body released the World Urbanization Prospects report using the Degree of Urbanization methodology?

options.text: UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Urbanization Prospects (WUP)** is a flagship publication produced by the **Population Division** of the **United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)**.
 
• The **2025 Revision** of this report represents a landmark shift as it is the first edition to fully implement the **Degree of Urbanization (DegUrba)** methodology for global comparative analysis.
 
• The **Degree of Urbanization** is a hierarchical classification that distinguishes the entire territory of a country into three main types of areas: **Cities**, **Towns and semi-dense areas**, and **Rural areas**.
 
• This methodology was formally endorsed by the **United Nations Statistical Commission** in **March 2020** during its **51st session** to harmonize the diverse and often incomparable national definitions of "urban" and "rural" areas.
 
• By using **population density** and **grid-based data** (typically **1 km² cells**), **UN DESA** aims to provide more consistent and accurate data on global urban trends, which is vital for international comparisons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)**: Established in **1948** and headquartered in **New York**, **USA**, it acts as a vital interface between global policies and national action. The **Population Division** within **UN DESA** provides the international community with up-to-date estimates and projections of population **age**, **location**, and **growth**.
 
• **World Urbanization Prospects (WUP)**: This series has been published since **1988**. It provides a comprehensive set of estimates and projections of the **urban** and **rural** populations of all countries in the world and of their major **urban agglomerations**.
 
• **UN-Habitat**: Based in **Nairobi**, **Kenya**, the **United Nations Human Settlements Programme** focuses on sustainable **urban development** and the implementation of the **New Urban Agenda**. While they collaborate on data, the primary statistical responsibility for the **WUP** report lies with **UN DESA**.
 
• **Global Urbanization Trends**: According to previous reports, **55%** of the world’s population lived in urban areas in **2018**, a figure that is projected to increase to **68%** by the year **2050**. Most of this growth is expected to take place in **Asia** and **Africa**.
 
• **Statistical Commission**: This is the highest body of the global statistical system, bringing together Chief Statisticians from **Member States**. It oversees the work of the **United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD)** and ensures that international standards like the **Degree of Urbanization** are adopted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of DegUrba**: Before the adoption of this methodology, countries used their own criteria (such as **administrative boundaries**, **population size**, or **economic functions**) to define urban areas, making it difficult to compare a city in **India** with a city in **France** or **Brazil**.
 
• **SDG Monitoring**: The use of standardized urbanization data by **UN DESA** is crucial for monitoring **Sustainable Development Goal 11 (SDG 11)**, which seeks to make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient, and sustainable by **2030**.
 
• **Leading Contributors to Growth**: It is estimated that just three countries—**India**, **China**, and **Nigeria**—will account for **35%** of the total growth in the world’s urban population between **2018** and **2050**. **India** is projected to add **416 million** urban dwellers.
 
• **Data Sources**: The report relies on **national census** data, **satellite imagery**, and **geospatial information** to refine the application of the **Degree of Urbanization** methodology across different **countries** and **continents**.

questions.question: In the Chola empire, the tax-free lands donated to Brahmins where they settled were known as __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agraharam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **Chola Empire**, which flourished between the **9th** and **13th century** in **South India**, the practice of donating **tax-free** lands to **Brahmins** was highly prevalent. These settlements were widely known as **Agraharam** or **Brahmadeya**.
 
• An **Agraharam** served as a residential quarter or a village where **Brahmins** settled to perform religious duties, Vedic education, and rituals. These lands were often situated near **temples** or fertile **river banks**.
 
• These land grants were exempted from the usual **land revenue** and other **taxes**, making them economically self-sufficient units. The primary **function** of these grants was to promote learning and sustain the priestly class.
 
• The internal **governance** of an **Agraharam** was managed by an assembly of Brahmin landowners known as the **Mahasabha**. This body looked after **irrigation**, **taxation** (if any), and the overall **administration** of the settlement.
 
• The **Chola** kings like **Rajaraja I** and **Rajendra I** frequently established these settlements to consolidate their **political influence** and propagate **Hinduism** throughout the **country**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Garbhagriha**: This is a prominent architectural **feature** of Hindu temples, referring to the **innermost sanctum** or "womb chamber" where the **primary deity** is installed. It was never a term used for land grants.
 
• **Valanadu**: In the **Chola** administrative system, the empire was divided into provinces called **Mandalam**, which were further divided into **Valanadu**. A **Valanadu** was a large administrative unit consisting of several **Nadu** (districts).
 
• **Mahasabha**: While often associated with **Agraharams**, the **Mahasabha** was the **assembly** or the **organisation** that governed the Brahmin settlements. It was the **administrative body** rather than the land itself.
 
• **Land Categories**: The **Chola** inscriptions mention several types of land holdings, such as **Vellanvagai** (land for non-Brahmin peasants), **Shalabhoga** (land for maintenance of schools), **Devadana** (land gifted to temples), and **Pallichchhandam** (land donated to Jain institutions).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Uttaramerur Inscription**: A famous inscription dated around **920 AD** during the reign of **Parantaka I** provides detailed **data** and **facts** about the election process of the **Sabha**. It highlights the use of the **Kuda-olai** (pot-ticket) system for choosing representatives.
 
• **Economic Impact**: These grants led to the **expansion of agriculture** in **South India** as Brahmins introduced new **irrigation techniques** and **management practices** to the donated **wastelands** or forest areas.
 
• **Role of the King**: The donation of **Agraharams** was a **political tool** used by the **Chola dynasty** to gain legitimacy and to create a loyal class of **intellectuals** who would record the **king's achievements** in Sanskrit and Tamil epigraphs.
 
• **Social Structure**: These settlements were exclusive **locations** for **Brahmins**, which occasionally led to a stratified **social hierarchy** in the **villages**, though they remained centers of great **cultural** and **intellectual** activity.

questions.question: Which of the following island groups in India is known to have an active volcano on Barren Island?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andaman and Nicobar Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Barren Island** is located in the **Andaman Sea** and is the only confirmed active volcano in **South Asia**. It is a part of the **Indian Union Territory** of the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**.
 
• The island is situated approximately **138 kilometers** (**86 miles**) northeast of **Port Blair**, the capital of the islands.
 
• The first recorded eruption of the volcano occurred in **1787**. After remaining dormant for about **150 years**, the volcano erupted again in **1991**, with the eruption lasting for **six months**.
 
• Recent volcanic activity on the island has been observed in **2005-07**, **2017**, and minor ash emissions were reported as recently as **2021**.
 
• The island is approximately **3 kilometers** wide, with a **2-kilometer-wide** caldera created during prehistoric explosive eruptions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands:**

 
 
• This archipelago consists of about **572 islands**, divided into the **Andaman** group in the north and the **Nicobar** group in the south, separated by the **Ten Degree Channel**.
 
• The highest point in the islands is **Saddle Peak**, which stands at an elevation of **732 meters** in **North Andaman**.
 
• The islands are home to **Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)** such as the **Jarawa**, **Sentinelese**, **Onge**, and **Great Andamanese**.
 
 
 
• **Lakshadweep Islands:**
 
 
• Located in the **Arabian Sea**, this is India's smallest **Union Territory**, consisting of **36 islands** with a total area of **32 square kilometers**.
 
• Unlike the volcanic Andaman islands, these are **coral islands** formed as **atolls**.
 
• The administrative headquarters is located at **Kavaratti**.
 
 
 
• **Narcondam Island:**
 
 
• Also located in the **Andaman Sea**, it is home to another volcano in India, which is currently classified as **dormant** or **extinct**.
 
• It is famous for the endemic **Narcondam Hornbill**, a bird species found nowhere else on **Earth**.
 
 
 
• **Minicoy and Rameswaram Islands:**
 
 
• **Minicoy Island** is the southernmost island of **Lakshadweep**, separated from the rest of the archipelago by the **Nine Degree Channel**.
 
• **Rameswaram Island** (also known as **Pamban Island**) is located between **mainland India** and **Sri Lanka** in the **Gulf of Mannar** and is connected to the mainland by the famous **Pamban Bridge**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tectonic Setting:** The volcanic activity in the **Andaman Sea** is a result of the subduction of the **Indian Plate** beneath the **Burmese Plate** (part of the **Eurasian Plate**) along the **Andaman Trench**.
 
• **Strategic Significance:** The **Andaman and Nicobar Command (ANC)**, established in **2001**, is India's first and only **tri-service theater command**, highlighting the region's immense strategic importance in the **Indian Ocean**.
 
• **Judicial Jurisdiction:** The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** fall under the legal jurisdiction of the **Calcutta High Court**, specifically the **Circuit Bench** at **Port Blair**.
 
• **Biodiversity:** The islands are part of the **Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot**, featuring tropical rainforests and extensive **mangrove** ecosystems that support diverse marine and terrestrial life.

questions.question:
Which statement is True or False regarding file management in Windows 11?

(i) When a file is deleted and moved to the Recycle Bin, its contents are immediately and permanently erased from the storage disk.

(ii) The file path (C: > Users > Documents > file.txt) is a strictly hierarchical structure, meaning each file has one unique path.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i) False, (ii) True**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement (i)**: When a file is deleted and moved to the **Recycle Bin** in **Windows 11**, its contents are not immediately erased. Instead, the file is simply moved to a hidden system folder, usually located at **$Recycle.Bin** on the root of each drive. The data remains physically present on the **storage disk** until the user chooses to **Empty the Recycle Bin** or the system automatically overwrites the space if it becomes critically low. *Hence, statement (i) is False.*
 
• **Statement (ii)**: The **file path** (e.g., **C: > Users > Documents > file.txt**) represents a **hierarchical structure** used by the **NTFS (New Technology File System)**. This organization resembles an inverted tree where the **Root Directory** (like **C:**) branches into **Subdirectories** (folders), and each individual file has a **unique absolute path** that defines its exact logical location within that hierarchy. *Hence, statement (ii) is True.*
 
• The **Recycle Bin** acts as a safety buffer, allowing users to restore **accidentally deleted** items to their **original location**. This feature has been a staple of the **Windows Operating System** since **Windows 95**.
 
• In **Windows 11**, the **File Explorer** manages these paths and provides a visual interface for navigating the **hierarchical data**. While a user can create a **Shortcut** to a file in multiple locations, the **source file** itself maintains only one **primary hierarchical path** on the disk.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Windows 11 File Management:**

 
 
• **Windows 11**, released in **October 2021**, introduced a redesigned **File Explorer** with **Tabs** and a simplified **context menu** to enhance productivity.
 
• The **NTFS** file system supports a maximum **path length** of **260 characters** by default, though this can be extended via **Registry** edits.
 
• **Metadata** such as **creation date**, **file size**, and **author name** are stored alongside the file in the **Master File Table (MFT)**.
 
 
 
• **Permanent Deletion:**
 
 
• To bypass the **Recycle Bin** and remove a file immediately, users can use the keyboard shortcut **Shift + Delete**.
 
• Even after **permanent deletion**, data recovery software can sometimes retrieve files unless the **storage blocks** have been **overwritten** by new data.
 
• On modern **Solid State Drives (SSDs)**, the **TRIM command** helps the **operating system** wipe data blocks more efficiently after permanent deletion to maintain performance.
 
 
 
• **Hierarchical vs. Flat File Systems:**
 
 
• A **Hierarchical file system** organizes data in a parent-child relationship, which is the standard for **Windows**, **macOS**, and **Linux**.
 
• Conversely, **Cloud Storage** (like **Amazon S3**) often uses a **Flat File System** where files (objects) are stored in a single layer and identified by unique **keys** rather than a nested folder path.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **File Extensions:** In **Windows 11**, the **extension** (e.g., **.txt**, **.docx**, **.exe**) tells the **operating system** which **application** should be used to open the file. By default, **File Explorer** may hide these **extensions** for known file types.
 
• **Logical vs. Physical Deletion:** Moving to the **Recycle Bin** is a **logical move**. The **physical data** remains on the **sectors** of the **Hard Disk Drive (HDD)** or **SSD** until the **logical link** is severed and the space is reused.
 
• **Storage Drive Letters:** In **India** and globally, most **PCs** assign **C:** as the **system drive** where **Windows 11** is installed, while additional **partitions** or **external drives** are assigned letters like **D:**, **E:**, or **F:**.
