questions.question: Which provision addresses citizenship for persons who migrated from Pakistan before India's Constitution commencement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 6** of the **Constitution of India** deals specifically with the rights of citizenship for persons who migrated to **India** from **Pakistan**. It provides that a person who migrated before the commencement of the Constitution shall be deemed a citizen if they or their parents/grandparents were born in undivided India. *Hence, this is the correct option.*
 
• **Article 5** outlines citizenship at the **commencement of the Constitution** (**January 26, 1950**) for individuals who had their domicile in India and were born in India, or whose parents were born in India, or who had been **ordinarily resident** for at least **five years**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Article 8** addresses the citizenship rights of certain persons of **Indian origin** residing **outside India**. It allows such individuals to become citizens if they are registered by the diplomatic or consular representative of India in the country where they are residing. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Article 10** ensures the **continuance of the rights of citizenship**. It states that every person who is considered a citizen under any of the preceding articles shall continue to be a citizen, subject to the provisions of any law made by the **Parliament**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:** **Part II** of the **Indian Constitution**, spanning from **Article 5 to Article 11**, defines who was eligible for Indian citizenship at the time of the Constitution's adoption.
 
• **Single Citizenship:** Unlike federal structures like the **USA**, India provides for **Single Citizenship**, meaning there is no separate state citizenship; all citizens owe allegiance only to the **Union of India**.
 
• **The Citizenship Act, 1955:** Since the constitutional provisions only dealt with citizenship at the time of commencement, the **Parliament** enacted the **Citizenship Act** in **1955** to regulate the **acquisition** and **loss** of citizenship after **1950**.
 
• **Acquisition Methods:** Under the **1955 Act**, citizenship can be acquired by **Birth**, **Descent**, **Registration**, **Naturalization**, and **Incorporation of Territory**.
 
• **Loss of Citizenship:** The Act also mentions three ways to lose citizenship: **Renunciation**, **Termination**, and **Deprivation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Cut-off Date:** For **Article 6**, the significant date is **July 19, 1948**. Individuals migrating before this date needed to be **ordinarily resident** in India since their migration to be deemed citizens.
 
• **Registration Requirement:** Those migrating from **Pakistan** on or after **July 19, 1948**, had to be registered as a citizen by an officer appointed by the **Government of the Dominion of India**, provided they had resided in India for at least **six months** prior to their application.
 
• **Article 7 (Migration to Pakistan):** This article deals with persons who migrated to **Pakistan** after **March 1, 1947**, but later returned to India under a **permit for resettlement** or permanent return; they could acquire citizenship similarly to those migrating after the 1948 cut-off.
 
• **Article 11 Power:** It gives **exclusive power** to the **Parliament of India** to make any law regarding citizenship. This ensures that the **Constitution** does not permanently limit the legislative scope of the government regarding who qualifies as an Indian national.
 
• **Ministry Involvement:** The **Ministry of Home Affairs** is the primary **government organization** responsible for overseeing citizenship, naturalization, and the **Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI)** scheme.

questions.question: Suman, Kunal, and Pooja invest ₹1050, ₹1510, and ₹1280 respectively to start a business. If the profit at the end of the year is ₹1650, then what is the share of Pooja in the profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit Ratio = Investment Ratio (since time is constant for all).

Ratio of Capitals (Suman : Kunal : Pooja) = 1050 : 1510 : 1280 = 105 : 151 : 128.

Total Ratio parts = 105 + 151 + 128 = 384 units.

Pooja's share = (128 ÷ 384) × Total Profit = 1/3 × 1650.

Pooja's share = 550.

**∴ Answer = 550**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Investment of Suman = ₹1050

Investment of Kunal = ₹1510

Investment of Pooja = ₹1280

Total Profit at the end of 1 year = ₹1650

**Formula used:**

Profit Ratio = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂) : (Capital₃ × Time₃)

 Investment Comparison ₹1050 Suman ₹1510 Kunal ₹1280 Pooja 
• Total Profit = ₹1650 

**Calculations:**

Ratio of Profit of Suman, Kunal, and Pooja = 1050 × 1 : 1510 × 1 : 1280 × 1

⇒ Profit Ratio = 105 : 151 : 128

⇒ Total ratio units = 105 + 151 + 128 = 384

⇒ Pooja's share in profit = (Ratio of Pooja ÷ Total Ratio) × Total Profit

⇒ Pooja's share = (128 ÷ 384) × 1650

⇒ Pooja's share = (1 ÷ 3) × 1650

⇒ Pooja's share = 550

**∴ The correct answer is ₹550.**

questions.question: A major characteristic of computer systems is Diligence. Which of the following scenarios primarily highlights a limitation of the computer system that is not overcome by its diligence?

options.text: A computer performs trillions of calculations a second, much faster than any human.
A computer generates incorrect output because the initial data entered was flawed.
A computer continues processing data for 72 hours straight without any loss of attention.
A computer is used to book flights in the morning and write code in the afternoon.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A computer generates incorrect output because the initial data entered was flawed.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diligence** is a core characteristic of a computer system that allows it to perform **repetitive tasks** for long periods without becoming tired, bored, or losing **concentration**. Unlike humans, who may suffer from physical or mental fatigue after working for a few hours, a computer remains consistent in its **performance**.
 
• Despite being diligent, a computer suffers from a significant **limitation** known as **Lack of IQ (Intelligence Quotient)**. A computer is a machine that follows instructions and cannot think, reason, or make judgments on its own; it requires a **human-defined program** to function.
 
• The scenario where a computer generates incorrect output due to flawed data refers to the **GIGO (Garbage In, Garbage Out)** principle. This highlights that while the computer is diligent enough to process the data, it lacks the **common sense** to identify that the input is incorrect. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• A computer performing **trillions of calculations** per second refers to the characteristic of **Speed**, which is measured in units like **MIPS (Million Instructions Per Second)** or **FLOPS (Floating Point Operations Per Second)**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The ability of a computer to continue processing for **72 hours straight** without losing attention is the definition of **Diligence** itself, rather than a limitation that diligence cannot overcome. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Using a computer for different tasks like **booking flights** and **writing code** highlights the characteristic of **Versatility**. This means the computer can be used in various **locations** such as **offices, airports, and schools** for diverse **applications**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Speed:** Computers are capable of executing **millions of instructions** in a fraction of a **second**. Modern **Supercomputers** can perform **quadrillions** of calculations per second. This **feature** makes them indispensable for **scientific research** and **weather forecasting**.
 
• **Accuracy:** If the **algorithms** and input data are correct, a computer provides **100% error-free** results. Errors usually occur due to **human intervention** or **incorrect programming**, not the machine's internal logic.
 
• **Storage (Versatility of Memory):** Computer systems have **huge storage capacities**. Data is stored in **bits and bytes** on devices like **Hard Disk Drives (HDD)**, **Solid State Drives (SSD)**, and **Cloud storage**. This allows for the **retention** of vast amounts of information for an indefinite **period**.
 
• **No Feelings:** Computers do not have **emotions**, tastes, or **intuition**. They cannot make **subjective decisions** based on **experience** or **feelings**, which is a major **limitation** compared to the human **brain**.
 
• **Dependency:** A computer is a **dependent machine**. It requires a **power source** and a **user** to provide **input**. Without **software** (instructions) and **hardware** (physical parts), the system is non-functional.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **GIGO (Garbage In, Garbage Out):** This term is fundamental in **Computer Science**. It emphasizes that the **reliability** of the output is strictly dependent on the **integrity** of the **input data**. For **organizations**, this means **data validation** is a critical step in **data processing**.
 
• **Evolution of Intelligence:** While traditional computers have **Zero IQ**, the **year** 1956 marked the formal beginning of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**. Modern AI aims to overcome the "No IQ" limitation by using **Machine Learning** and **Neural Networks** to mimic human **decision-making**.
 
• **Reliability:** Because computers are **diligent** and **accurate**, they are considered highly **reliable**. They are used in critical **functions** like **space exploration** (NASA/ISRO), **medical surgeries**, and **global banking** systems where **consistency** is vital.

questions.question: Which of the following introduced dyarchy by dividing subjects into Reserved and Transferred lists?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act, 1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1919**, also known as the **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**, introduced a system called **Dyarchy** in the provinces of **British India**.
 
• Under this system of **Dyarchy**, the provincial subjects of administration were divided into two distinct categories: **Reserved Subjects** and **Transferred Subjects**.
 
• **Reserved Subjects**: These included vital departments such as **Law and Order**, **Finance**, **Land Revenue**, and **Police**. These subjects were administered by the **Governor** with the help of his **Executive Council**, without being responsible to the **Legislative Council**.
 
• **Transferred Subjects**: These included departments like **Education**, **Public Health**, **Local Self-Government**, and **Agriculture**. These were administered by the **Governor** with the aid of **Ministers** who were responsible to the **Legislative Council**.
 
• This Act marked the first time that the **British Government** officially declared its objective of gradual introduction of **responsible government** in India.
 
• The Act also introduced **Bicameralism** at the center for the first time, consisting of an **Upper House** (Council of State) and a **Lower House** (Legislative Assembly).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Councils Act, 1892**:

 
 
• This Act increased the number of **additional (non-official) members** in the **Central and Provincial Legislative Councils**.
 
• It increased the functions of **Legislative Councils** and gave them the power of **discussing the budget** and addressing questions to the executive.
 
• It provided for the **nomination** of some non-official members, introducing a limited and indirect use of **election** in filling up some of the non-official seats.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms)**:
 
 
• This Act is significantly known for introducing **Separate Electorates** for **Muslims**, thereby legalizing **communalism** in Indian politics.
 
• It considerably increased the size of the **Legislative Councils** at both the **Central** and **Provincial** levels.
 
• For the first time, it provided for the association of **Indians** with the **Executive Councils** of the **Viceroy** and **Governors**; **Satyendra Prasad Sinha** became the first Indian to join the Viceroy’s Executive Council as a **Law Member**.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935**:
 
 
• This Act abolished **Dyarchy** in the provinces and introduced **Provincial Autonomy** in its place.
 
• However, it provided for the adoption of **Dyarchy at the Centre**, dividing federal subjects into **Reserved** and **Transferred** (though this provision never came into operation).
 
• It provided for the establishment of an **All-India Federation** consisting of provinces and **princely states** as units.
 
• It also led to the establishment of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **1935** and a **Federal Court** in **1937**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **1919 Act** was based on the report submitted by **Edwin Montagu**, the then **Secretary of State for India**, and **Lord Chelmsford**, the **Viceroy of India**.
 
• It mandated that **three of the six members** of the **Viceroy’s Executive Council** (other than the Commander-in-Chief) were to be **Indians**.
 
• The Act extended the principle of **communal representation** by providing separate electorates for **Sikhs**, **Indian Christians**, **Anglo-Indians**, and **Europeans**.
 
• It granted a **limited franchise** to people on the basis of **property, tax, or education**.
 
• It also provided for the establishment of a **Public Service Commission**, leading to the setting up of a **Central Public Service Commission** in **1926** for recruiting civil servants.
 
• The **Simon Commission** was appointed in **November 1927** (two years ahead of schedule) to report on the working of the reforms introduced by the **Act of 1919**.

questions.question: 100 men have provisions for 26 days. If 50 men have left, for how many days the same provisions would last for the remaining men?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Men ratio = 100 : 50 = 2 : 1

Days ratio = 1 : 2 (Inverse of Men ratio because Total Provision is constant)

1 unit = 26 days

2 units = 26 × 2 = 52 days

**∴ Answer = 52**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Initial number of men (M₁) = 100

Initial number of days (D₁) = 26

Number of men who left = 50

Remaining men (M₂) = 100 − 50 = 50

**Formula used:**

M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂ (Chain Rule when work/provision is constant)

 Initial: 100 Men D1 = 26 Days Final: 50 Men (Left 50) D2 = 52 Days 
 Inverse Relation Men ÷ 2 → Days × 2 Total Provision = 2600 units 

**Calculations:**

Total provision = M₁ × D₁ = 100 × 26 = 2600 man-days

⇒ 2600 = M₂ × D₂

⇒ 2600 = 50 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = 2600 ÷ 50

⇒ D₂ = 52

**∴ The correct answer is 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

General Chain Rule (MDH Rule)

The relationship between men (M), days (D), hours (H), and work (W) is given by (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) / W₂.

Inverse Proportion

In provision problems, the number of men is inversely proportional to the number of days the food lasts, provided the consumption per man remains constant.

Provision Addition Case

If more men join, the provisions will last for fewer days. New Days = (Initial Men × Initial Days) ÷ (Initial Men + New Men).

questions.question: Jaspreet deposited a sum of ₹28,450 at 20% rate of interest per annum, compounded annually. The total amount received by Jaspreet after 2 years is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective interest rate for 2 years at 20% per annum = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20) ÷ 100 = 44%

Total amount percentage = 100% (Principal) + 44% (Interest) = 144%

Total amount = 144% of 28,450

Total amount = 1.44 × 28,450 = 40,968

**∴ Answer = 40,968**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹28,450

Rate of Interest (R) = 20% per annum

Time (n) = 2 years

**Formula used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 
• Year 0 Year 1 Year 2 ₹28,450 
 +20% CI 
 +20% CI ₹40,968 
 

**Calculations:**

A = 28,450 × (1 + 20/100)²

⇒ A = 28,450 × (1 + 1/5)²

⇒ A = 28,450 × (6/5)²

⇒ A = 28,450 × (36/25)

⇒ A = 1,138 × 36

⇒ A = 40,968

**∴ The correct answer is ₹40,968.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Interest

For compound interest, the effective rate for two years can be calculated using the successive percentage formula: x + y + (xy/100)%.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference (D) between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is given by: D = P(R/100)².

Compounding Periods

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate becomes R/2 and the time becomes 2n. If compounded quarterly, the rate is R/4 and time is 4n.

Rule of 72

To find the approximate time required to double your money with compound interest, divide 72 by the annual interest rate: T ≈ 72 ÷ R.

questions.question: Who among the following established the famous Nrityagram institution in Bengaluru?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protima Gauri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Protima Gauri** (widely known as **Protima Bedi**) was the visionary who established **Nrityagram**, which is India's first modern **Gurukul** or residential dance village. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• The institution was founded in the **year 1990** and is situated in **Hessaraghatta**, located on the outskirts of **Bengaluru**, **Karnataka**.
 
• The primary objective of **Nrityagram** is to provide a space where **Indian classical dance** forms can be practiced as a way of life, following the ancient **Gurukul system** where students live with their mentors.
 
• The institution is globally recognized for its excellence in **Odissi**, though it has also hosted training in other classical forms like **Mohiniyattam**, **Kathak**, **Bharatnatyam**, and **Kuchipudi**.
 
• The village was built on **10 acres** of land provided by the **Government of Karnataka** on lease, fulfilling **Protima Gauri's** dream of creating a self-sustaining community of artists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Protima Gauri:** Born in **1948**, she was a celebrated **model** and **socialite** in **Mumbai** before transitioning into a dedicated **Odissi dancer** after witnessing a performance by **Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra**. She spent her later years building and nurturing **Nrityagram** until her passing in **1998**.
 
• **Surupa Sen:** She was the first student to join **Nrityagram** and currently serves as the **Artistic Director**. She is an acclaimed **choreographer** and dancer who has significantly expanded the **Odissi** vocabulary through her compositions. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect as she is a leader of the institution but not the founder.***
 
• **Bijayini Satpathy:** She is a world-renowned **Odissi** performer who was associated with **Nrityagram** for **25 years** as its principal dancer and **Director of the Odissi Gurukul**. She is credited with refining the training pedagogy at the village. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Pavithra Reddy:** A prominent dancer and **teacher** at **Nrityagram**, she joined the institution through its **rural outreach program** and has since become one of its lead performers. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Geographical Location:** **Hessaraghatta** is located about **30 kilometers** from the city center of **Bengaluru** and is also known for the **Hessaraghatta Lake** and various agricultural research institutes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Architecture:** The **Nrityagram** campus was designed by the award-winning architect **Gerard da Cunha**. The design is unique for its use of **raw earth**, **thatch**, and **indigenous materials**, winning the **Rural Architecture Award** in **1991**.
 
• **Vasanthahabba:** This was a famous **all-night spring festival** of arts started by **Protima Gauri** in **1990**. It was often called the **Woodstock of India**, drawing thousands of urban and rural spectators to witness world-class dance and music performances for free.
 
• **Training Philosophy:** Students at **Nrityagram** undergo a rigorous **six-year** full-time residency. The training involves **Yoga**, **Kalaripayattu** (martial arts), **Sanskrit**, and **literature**, alongside intensive dance practice to ensure a holistic development of the artist.
 
• **Global Impact:** The **Nrityagram Dance Ensemble** has performed at prestigious international venues like the **Joyce Theater** in **New York** and the **Edinburgh International Festival**, bringing global attention to Indian heritage.

questions.question: The Tamil literary work Iraiyanar Ahapporul is dated to which century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8th century CE**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Iraiyanar Ahapporul**, also frequently referred to as **Iraiyanar Kalaviyal**, is a seminal work in **Tamil** literature that focuses on the grammar of love or **Agam** poetry.
 
• Most historians and literary scholars date the compilation and its famous commentary to the **8th century CE**. While the core **60 sutras** are sometimes traditionally attributed to an earlier period, the definitive version used by scholars includes the commentary by **Nakkirar**, which was finalized around this time.
 
• The work is of immense historical value because it contains the first-ever detailed mention of the **Three Tamil Sangams** (literary academies). It outlines the chronology, the **Pandyan** kings who patronized them, and the duration of each **Sangam**.
 
• The text serves as a foundational bridge between the **Sangam Era** (3rd century BCE to 3rd century CE) and the later medieval period of **Tamil** linguistic evolution. It helped systematize the rules of **Agam** (internal/romantic) literature, which was a dominant theme in ancient **Tamil** culture.
 
• The **8th century CE** date is supported by the linguistic style of the prose commentary, which represents an early form of developed **Tamil** prose, and references to **Pandyan** monarchs like **Arikesari Parankusa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure and Themes**: The **Iraiyanar Ahapporul** consists of **60 short verses** or **sutras**. These verses are exclusively dedicated to **Kalaviyal**, which deals with the clandestine or pre-marital phase of love, a core component of **Agam** literature.
 
• **The Legend of Authorship**: According to **Tamil** tradition, during a severe famine in the **Pandyan** kingdom, the scholars of the **Sangam** dispersed. When they returned, the knowledge of **Ahapporul** (the grammar of love) was lost. It is believed that **Lord Shiva** (Iraiyanar) composed these **60 sutras** and left them under his seat in the **Madurai** temple to restore the literary tradition.
 
• **Nakkirar’s Commentary**: The commentary on this work is as famous as the text itself. **Nakkirar**, a renowned poet, is credited with writing the exhaustive explanation. It is widely considered the **first major prose work** in the **Tamil language**, setting a precedent for future commentators.
 
• **The Three Sangams**: The text claims that the **First Sangam** (Mudal Sangam) was held at **Thenmadurai**, the **Second Sangam** (Idai Sangam) at **Kapatapuram**, and the **Third Sangam** (Kadai Sangam) at the modern city of **Madurai**. Although the timeframes mentioned (thousands of years) are considered mythical by modern historians, the sequence provides a framework for understanding **Tamil** literary history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Linguistic Significance**: Before the **Iraiyanar Ahapporul**, the primary source for **Tamil** grammar was the **Tolkappiyam**. This **8th-century** work refined the **Agam** conventions specifically for the post-Sangam audience.
 
• **Patronage**: The commentary mentions **Pandyan** kings, which helps in cross-referencing the date. The mentions of the **Pandyan** king **Nedumaran** and battle victories at places like **Pali** and **Sennilam** are crucial for **archaeological** and **epigraphical** dating.
 
• **Cultural Impact**: It solidified the "five landscapes" (**Ainthinai**) theory of **Tamil** poetry, where different geographical locations (**Kurinji, Mullai, Marutham, Neithal, Palai**) are associated with specific moods of love.
 
• **Preservation**: The survival of this text ensured that the legends of the **Sangam** were passed down to later generations, eventually leading to the modern **Tamil Renaissance** in the **19th** and **20th centuries**.

questions.question: The price of fuel decreases by 40%, 60% and 60% in three successive months, but increases by 70% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase or decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive multipliers: 0.60 (40% decrease), 0.40 (60% decrease), 0.40 (60% decrease), and 1.70 (70% increase).

Net Multiplier = 0.60 × 0.40 × 0.40 × 1.70 = 0.1632

Final Price = 100% × 0.1632 = 16.32%

Net Change = 100% − 16.32% = 83.68% decrease.

**∴ Answer = Decrease by 83.68%** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Price changes: Month 1 = −40%, Month 2 = −60%, Month 3 = −60%, Month 4 = +70%.

**Formula used:**

Final Price = Initial Price × (1 − r₁/100) × (1 − r₂/100) × (1 − r₃/100) × (1 + r₄/100)

 
• 100 Original 
 -40% 60 
 -60% 24 
 -60% 9.6 
 +70% 16.32 Final Total Decrease = 83.68% 

**Calculations:**

Let the original price be 100.

⇒ Price after 1st month = 100 × (1 − 40/100) = 100 × 0.60 = 60

⇒ Price after 2nd month = 60 × (1 − 60/100) = 60 × 0.40 = 24

⇒ Price after 3rd month = 24 × (1 − 60/100) = 24 × 0.40 = 9.6

⇒ Price after 4th month = 9.6 × (1 + 70/100) = 9.6 × 1.70 = 16.32

⇒ Total decrease = 100 − 16.32 = 83.68

⇒ Percentage decrease = (83.68 ÷ 100) × 100 = 83.68%

**∴ The correct answer is Decrease by 83.68%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

For two successive changes of x% and y%, the net effective change is [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Multiplying Factor Method

Final Value = Initial Value × Multiplier. For a p% increase, multiplier = (1 + p/100). For a p% decrease, multiplier = (1 − p/100).

Depreciation Formula

Value after n years = P(1 − r/100)ⁿ, where P is the initial value and r is the constant rate of decrease.

questions.question: Which system has become a cornerstone of government development policy and is tied to most rural development programs?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Empowerment Scheme (MGNRES)
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** was passed in **August 2005** and officially launched on **February 2, 2006**, initially covering **200** of the most backward districts in India.
 
• It is considered a **cornerstone** of development policy because it shifted the approach from **welfare-based** to **rights-based**, providing a **legal guarantee** for at least **100 days** of wage employment in a **financial year** to every rural household whose adult members volunteer for **unskilled manual work**.
 
• The scheme is a **demand-driven** program, meaning the government is legally bound to provide work within **15 days** of a demand being made, failing which an **unemployment allowance** must be paid to the applicant.
 
• It is tied to most rural development programs as it creates **durable assets** such as **check dams**, **ponds**, **wells**, and **rural roads**, which are essential for long-term agricultural and infrastructural growth.
 
• The **Ministry of Rural Development**, Government of India, monitors the entire implementation of this scheme in association with **State Governments**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Public Distribution System (PDS):**

 
 
• The **PDS** is an Indian food security system established under the **Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food, and Public Distribution**.
 
• It focuses on distributing essential foodgrains like **wheat** and **rice**, and non-food items like **kerosene**, to the poor at subsidized rates through a network of **Fair Price Shops (FPS)**.
 
• The **National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013**, further strengthened this by providing legal entitlement to **75%** of the rural and **50%** of the urban population.
 
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan:**
 
 
• Launched on **October 2, 2014**, by the Prime Minister to honor the **150th birth anniversary** of **Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
• It aims to achieve universal **sanitation coverage** and make India **Open Defecation Free (ODF)** by constructing individual and community toilets.
 
• The mission has two thrusts: **Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin)** for rural areas and **Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban)**.
 
 
 
• **MGNRES (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Empowerment Scheme):**
 
 
• Note that "MGNRES" is often a misnomer or a slight variation in terminology; the official legal name remains **MGNREGA**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Social Audit:** MGNREGA mandates a **Social Audit** by the **Gram Sabha** at least once every **six months**, which is a powerful tool for ensuring **transparency** and **accountability** in the expenditure of funds.
 
• **Women Empowerment:** The Act stipulates that at least **one-third (33%)** of the beneficiaries shall be **women** who have registered and requested for work under the scheme.
 
• **Funding:** The **Central Government** bears **100%** of the cost of **unskilled manual labor** and **75%** of the material cost, while the **State Governments** contribute the remaining **25%** of the material cost and the **unemployment allowance**.
 
• **Financial Inclusion:** Wages are paid directly into the **Bank accounts** or **Post Office accounts** of the workers using the **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** mechanism to prevent leakages and corruption.
 
• **Coverage:** Since **April 1, 2008**, the act has been extended to cover **all rural districts** of the country, making it a universal program for the rural poor.

questions.question:
Solve the following system of 3 equations in 3 unknowns.

x − 3z = −5

2x − y + 2z = 16

7x − 3y − 5z = 19
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Substitution method: Test given options in the simplest equation, x − 3z = −5.

Check Option (4): x = 4, y = −2, z = 3.

Eq (1): 4 − 3(3) = 4 − 9 = −5 (Correct).

Eq (2): 2(4) − (−2) + 2(3) = 8 + 2 + 6 = 16 (Correct).

Eq (3): 7(4) − 3(−2) − 5(3) = 28 + 6 − 15 = 19 (Correct).

**∴ Answer = Option (4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

x − 3z = −5 ...(i)

2x − y + 2z = 16 ...(ii)

7x − 3y − 5z = 19 ...(iii)

**Formula used:**

Method of Elimination and Substitution.

 Eq (i): x − 3z = −5 Eq (ii): 2x − y + 2z = 16 Eq (iii): 7x − 3y − 5z = 19 
 Solution: x = 4, y = −2, z = 3 Option (4) 

**Calculations:**

From (i), x = 3z − 5.

Substitute x in (ii): 2(3z − 5) − y + 2z = 16

⇒ 6z − 10 − y + 2z = 16 ⇒ y = 8z − 26 ...(iv)

Substitute x and y in (iii): 7(3z − 5) − 3(8z − 26) − 5z = 19

⇒ 21z − 35 − 24z + 78 − 5z = 19

⇒ −8z + 43 = 19 ⇒ −8z = −24 ⇒ z = 3

⇒ x = 3(3) − 5 = 4

⇒ y = 8(3) − 26 = −2

**∴ The correct answer is Option (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cramer's Rule

Variables are solved using determinants: x = Dₓ/D, y = Dy/D, and z = Dz/D, provided D ≠ 0.

Matrix Method

The system AX = B is solved as X = A−¹B, where A is the coefficient matrix.

Consistency of System

A system is consistent if rank(A) = rank(A|B). It has a unique solution if this rank equals the number of variables.

questions.question: The formation of a spectrum by a glass prism occurs due to ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dispersion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dispersion** is the phenomenon of splitting **white light** into its constituent seven colors when it passes through a transparent medium like a **glass prism**. Hence, the formation of a spectrum is primarily due to this process.
 
• The spectrum consists of seven colors, commonly remembered by the acronym **VIBGYOR**: **Violet**, **Indigo**, **Blue**, **Green**, **Yellow**, **Orange**, and **Red**.
 
• The splitting occurs because different colors of light travel at different **speeds** in a glass medium, even though they travel at the same speed in a **vacuum**. This variation in speed leads to different **refractive indices** for each color.
 
• **Sir Isaac Newton** was the first scientist to use a glass prism in **1666** to demonstrate that sunlight is made up of seven colors. He showed that if a second inverted prism is placed in the path of the spectrum, the colors recombine to form white light again.
 
• In the process of dispersion, **Violet light** undergoes the maximum deviation because it has the **shortest wavelength**, while **Red light** undergoes the minimum deviation because it has the **longest wavelength**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Refraction**:

 
 
• This is the bending of light when it passes from one **optical medium** to another of different **optical density**. It occurs due to the change in the **velocity** of light.
 
• While refraction is the mechanism that causes the light to bend at the surfaces of the prism, the specific separation into colors is called dispersion. *Hence, statement 2 is the underlying mechanism but not the specific answer for spectrum formation.*
 
 
 
• **Reflection**:
 
 
• This is the phenomenon where light rays **bounce back** into the same medium after striking a polished or shiny surface, like a **mirror**.
 
• It follows two laws: the **angle of incidence** equals the **angle of reflection**, and the incident ray, reflected ray, and the **normal** all lie in the same plane. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect as it does not result in a spectrum in this context.*
 
 
 
• **Scattering**:
 
 
• This occurs when light rays are deviated from their straight path upon striking obstacles like **dust particles**, gas molecules, or water droplets.
 
• The **blue color of the sky** and the **reddish appearance of the sun** at sunrise and sunset are due to **Rayleigh scattering**. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect regarding the prism's spectrum.*
 
 
 
• **Rainbow Formation**:
 
 
• A natural spectrum appearing in the sky after rain is a **rainbow**. It is caused by the **dispersion** of sunlight by tiny **water droplets**, which act like small prisms.
 
• The process involves three steps: **refraction**, internal **dispersion**, and **total internal reflection** within the raindrop.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Angle of Deviation**: The angle between the **incident ray** and the **emergent ray** is known as the angle of deviation. In a prism, this angle depends on the **angle of the prism** and the **refractive index** of the material.
 
• **Wavelength and Frequency**: The **wavelength** (λ) of light is inversely proportional to its frequency and the refractive index of the medium. Visible light ranges roughly from **400 nm** (Violet) to **700 nm** (Red).
 
• **Cauchy's Formula**: This mathematical relation describes how the refractive index of a material varies with the wavelength of light, explaining why different colors refract at different angles, leading to **dispersion**.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**92nd Amendment Act, 2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **92nd Constitutional Amendment Act** was enacted in the year **2003** to amend the **Eighth Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• This specific amendment added four new languages to the list of official languages: **Bodo**, **Dogri**, **Maithili**, and **Santhali**.
 
• With the inclusion of these four languages, the total number of languages listed in the **Eighth Schedule** increased from **18** to **22**.
 
• The bill for this amendment received the **President's assent** on **January 7, 2004**, and it became effective from that period.
 
• The **92nd Amendment** is significant as it recognized the linguistic diversity and cultural identity of the speakers of these languages, primarily located in **Assam** (Bodo), **Jammu and Kashmir** (Dogri), **Bihar** (Maithili), and **Jharkhand/West Bengal** (Santhali).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **86th Amendment Act, 2002**:

 
 
• This amendment is primarily related to **Education**. It inserted **Article 21A** into the Constitution, making the **Right to Education** a **Fundamental Right** for children aged **6 to 14 years**.
 
• It also amended **Article 45** (Directive Principles) and added a new **Fundamental Duty** under **Article 51A(k)** for parents to provide opportunities for education to their children.
 
 
 
• **91st Amendment Act, 2003**:
 
 
• This amendment dealt with the size of the **Council of Ministers** and the **Anti-Defection Law**.
 
• It stipulated that the total number of ministers, including the **Prime Minister**, in the Central Council of Ministers shall not exceed **15%** of the total strength of the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• A similar provision was applied to the **State Legislative Assemblies**, ensuring that the number of ministers (including the **Chief Minister**) does not exceed **15%** of the total strength of the Assembly, with a minimum of **12** ministers.
 
 
 
• **93rd Amendment Act, 2005**:
 
 
• This amendment allowed the **State** to make special provisions for the advancement of any socially and educationally **Backward Classes** or for the **Scheduled Castes** or the **Scheduled Tribes** regarding their admission to **educational institutions**.
 
• This includes **private educational institutions**, whether aided or unaided by the State, except for **minority educational institutions** referred to in **Article 30(1)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of the Eighth Schedule**:

 
 
• The **Constitution** originally listed **14** languages in the **Eighth Schedule** in **1950**.
 
• The **21st Amendment Act, 1967**, added **Sindhi** as the **15th** language.
 
• The **71st Amendment Act, 1992**, added three more languages: **Konkani**, **Manipuri**, and **Nepali**, bringing the count to **18**.
 
• The **92nd Amendment Act, 2003**, added the final four (**Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali**), resulting in the current total of **22**.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Articles**:
 
 
• **Article 344(1)** provides for the constitution of a **Commission** by the President on expiration of **five years** from the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• **Article 351** provides a directive for the development of the **Hindi language** so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all the elements of the composite culture of **India**.
 
 
 
• **Current Status**: At present, there are **22** scheduled languages in India. These include Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Oriya, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, **Bodo**, **Santhali**, **Maithili**, and **Dogri**.

questions.question: Who among the following was a prominent disciple of Ramanuja’s Sri Vaishnava tradition who played a significant role in spreading its Bhakti teachings to North India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ramananda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ramananda** was a **14th-century** Vaishnava devotional poet-saint who lived in the **Gangetic basin** of northern India. He is widely recognized as the primary figure who brought the **Bhakti movement** from South India to **North India**.
 
• He was a devoted follower of the **Sri Vaishnava** tradition, which was originally pioneered by **Ramanujacharya**. However, Ramananda introduced significant reforms to make the tradition more accessible to the masses.
 
• One of his most revolutionary contributions was preaching in **Hindi**, the **vernacular language** of the common people, instead of **Sanskrit**. This shift allowed the **Bhakti teachings** to reach a much wider audience across the northern plains.
 
• **Ramananda** is also credited with discarding the rigid **caste rules** within the spiritual domain. He famously declared, "Let no man ask a man’s caste or sect; whoever adores God is God’s own."
 
• He founded the **Ramanandi Sampradaya**, which remains one of the largest **monastic orders** in India today, centered primarily in **Ayodhya** and **Varanasi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ramanujacharya (1017–1137 AD)**:

 
 
• He was a great philosopher and social reformer from **Tamil Nadu**. He propounded the philosophy of **Vishishtadvaita** (qualified monism).
 
• He revitalized the **Sri Vaishnava** movement and is the original inspiration behind the lineage that **Ramananda** later adapted for North India.
 
 
 
• **Madhvacharya (1238–1317 AD)**:
 
 
• He was a philosopher from the **Karnataka** region and the founder of the **Dvaita** (dualism) school of Vedanta.
 
• He was a staunch critic of **Shankara's Advaita** and **Ramanuja's Vishishtadvaita**, emphasizing the absolute distinction between **Brahman** (God) and individual souls.
 
 
 
• **Namdev (1270–1350 AD)**:
 
 
• He was a prominent saint from **Maharashtra** belonging to the **Varkari** tradition.
 
• While he played a role in spreading **Bhakti** and his hymns are even included in the **Guru Granth Sahib**, he was primarily associated with the worship of **Lord Vitthal** (a form of Vishnu) in the **Deccan** region.
 
 
 
• **Bhakti Movement**:
 
 
• The movement began in **South India** in the **7th to 9th centuries** through the **Alvars** (devotees of Vishnu) and **Nayanars** (devotees of Shiva).

Which of the following apparent forces, caused by Earth’s rotation, deflects winds to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coriolis force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Coriolis force** is an **apparent force** caused by the **Earth's rotation** on its axis. It is not a real force in the sense of a physical push or pull but is an effect observed because the Earth rotates beneath the moving air or water.
 
• According to **Ferrel's Law**, this force deflects moving objects, such as **wind and ocean currents**, to the **right** of their path in the **Northern Hemisphere** and to the **left** in the **Southern Hemisphere**.
 
• The magnitude of the **Coriolis force** is directly proportional to the **sine of the latitude**. Therefore, it is **zero at the Equator** and reaches its **maximum at the North and South Poles**.
 
• This force acts **perpendicular** to the direction of the wind and the pressure gradient force. It plays a critical role in the **general circulation of the atmosphere** and the formation of **cyclonic weather systems**.
 
• It was first mathematically described by the **French scientist Gaspard-Gustave de Coriolis** in the **year 1835**. He explained how energy transfer in rotating systems affects the motion of bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pressure Gradient Force (PGF):**

 
 
• This force is generated by **differences in atmospheric pressure** between two regions. It acts from **high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas**.
 
• The **rate of change of pressure** with respect to distance is known as the pressure gradient. When **isobars** (lines of equal pressure) are close together, the gradient is **steep** and the wind speed is **high**.
 
• While PGF initiates the movement of air, the **Coriolis force** subsequently modifies its direction.
 
 
 
• **Frictional Force:**
 
 
• This force **opposes the motion** of the wind and is most significant near the **Earth's surface**. It generally affects wind up to an **altitude of 1 to 3 kilometers**, a layer known as the **planetary boundary layer**.
 
• Over **oceans**, the friction is **minimal**, allowing winds to be stronger, whereas over **mountainous or forested land**, friction is **maximum**.
 
• Friction slows down the wind, which in turn **reduces the Coriolis effect**, causing the wind to blow more across the isobars toward low pressure rather than parallel to them.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Force:**
 
 
• **Gravity** acts **downward** toward the center of the Earth. It prevents the atmosphere from escaping into space and creates **vertical pressure gradients**.
 
• While it is a fundamental force, its direct contribution to the **horizontal deflection** of winds is negligible compared to the **Coriolis force**.
 
 
 
• **Geostrophic Wind:**
 
 
• In the **upper atmosphere** (above the friction layer), when the **Pressure Gradient Force** and the **Coriolis force** are in **equilibrium**, the resulting wind blows **parallel to the isobars**. This is called the **Geostrophic wind**.
 
• This phenomenon explains the characteristic flow of the **Jet Streams** and other high-altitude wind patterns.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact on Cyclones:** In the **Northern Hemisphere**, the Coriolis force causes winds to blow **counter-clockwise** around a **low-pressure center** (cyclone). In the **Southern Hemisphere**, the rotation is **clockwise**.
 
• **Wind Speed Factor:** The Coriolis force is also dependent on the **speed of the wind**. The **faster** the wind blows, the **stronger** the deflection caused by the Coriolis effect.
 
• **Equatorial Absence:** Because the Coriolis force is **absent at 0 degrees latitude**, **tropical cyclones** rarely form between **5 degrees North and 5 degrees South** of the Equator; there is insufficient "spin" to initiate the cyclonic rotation.

questions.question: If the equations x² – 3px + q = 0 and x² – 2kx + t = 0 have one common root, and the first equation has equal roots, what is the value of (t + q)²?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For x² − 3px + q = 0 with equal roots, each root is −(−3p)/2 = 3p/2.

Product of equal roots: (3p/2) × (3p/2) = q ⇒ q = 9p²/4.

The common root must be 3p/2. Substitute it into x² − 2kx + t = 0.

(3p/2)² − 2k(3p/2) + t = 0 ⇒ q − 3pk + t = 0.

This gives (t + q) = 3pk. Squaring both sides, we get (t + q)² = 9p²k².

**∴ Answer = 9p²k²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation 1: x² − 3px + q = 0 has equal roots.

Equation 2: x² − 2kx + t = 0 share one root with Equation 1.

**Formula used:**

For ax² + bx + c = 0, if roots are equal, then Discriminant D = b² − 4ac = 0 and root x = −b/2a.

 Eq 1: Roots (α, α) Eq 2: Roots (α, β) α = 3p/2 
• q = (3p/2)² t + q = 3pk

**Calculations:**

For x² − 3px + q = 0, equal roots mean (−3p)² − 4(1)(q) = 0

⇒ 9p² = 4q ⇒ q = 9p²/4.

⇒ The equal roots are α = −(−3p)/2 = 3p/2.

⇒ Since Eq 1 and Eq 2 have a common root, x = 3p/2 must satisfy x² − 2kx + t = 0.

⇒ (3p/2)² − 2k(3p/2) + t = 0

⇒ 9p²/4 − 3pk + t = 0

⇒ q − 3pk + t = 0 (Substituting q = 9p²/4)

⇒ t + q = 3pk

⇒ Squaring both sides: (t + q)² = (3pk)² = 9p²k².

**∴ The correct answer is 9p²k² (Option 1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Condition for One Common Root

For a₁x² + b₁x + c₁ = 0 and a₂x² + b₂x + c₂ = 0, the condition for one root common is (a₁c₂ − a₂c₁)² = (b₁c₂ − b₂c₁)(a₁b₂ − a₂b₁).

Condition for Both Roots Common

Two quadratic equations have both roots common if their coefficients are proportional: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

Nature of Roots

If D = b² − 4ac > 0, roots are real and distinct; if D = 0, roots are real and equal; if D < 0, roots are imaginary.

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT directly associated with the Prarthana Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Debendranath Tagore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prarthana Samaj** was a movement for **religious and social reform** in **Bombay**, India, founded in **1867**. It was inspired by the **Brahmo Samaj** and sought to reform **Hinduism** from within.
 
• **Atmaram Pandurang** was the **founder** of the **Prarthana Samaj**. He established the organization on **31 March 1867** with the help of **Keshab Chandra Sen**, a prominent leader of the **Brahmo Samaj**.
 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade** (popularly known as **M.G. Ranade**) joined the **Samaj** in **1870**. He was the **primary figure** who popularized the movement and expanded its **social reform** activities across **Maharashtra**.
 
• **R.C. Bhandarkar** (also known as **Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar**) was a renowned **orientalist** and **scholar** who was a **founding member** and a pillar of the **Prarthana Samaj**. He provided the **theological** and **intellectual** foundation for the movement.
 
• **Debendranath Tagore** was a leader of the **Brahmo Samaj** in **Bengal** and founded the **Tattvabodhini Sabha** in **1839**. While his work influenced movements across India, he was **not directly associated** with the **Prarthana Samaj** in **Bombay**. ***Hence, Debendranath Tagore is the correct option.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Social Reforms:** The **Prarthana Samaj** focused on **social justice**, including the **abolition of the caste system**, the **promotion of women's education**, and **widow remarriage**. It also campaigned against **child marriage** and **untouchability**.
 
• **Religious Philosophy:** Unlike the **Brahmo Samaj**, the **Prarthana Samaj** did not seek to form a new religion but remained within the **Hindu fold**. It emphasized **monotheism** and the **worship of one God** through **prayer** and **bhakti** (devotion), drawing inspiration from **Marathi saint-poets** like **Namdev** and **Tukaram**.
 
• **Institutions:** Under the leadership of **M.G. Ranade**, the **Samaj** established various institutions, such as **orphanages**, **night schools** for the working class, and **asylums**. In **1861**, **Ranade** helped found the **Widow Marriage Association**.
 
• **Influence of Keshab Chandra Sen:** The organization was heavily influenced by **Keshab Chandra Sen’s** visit to **Bombay** in **1864**. His **progressive ideas** and **eloquent speeches** motivated local intellectuals to start a **reformist society**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Location and Reach:** The **Prarthana Samaj** was primarily based in the **Bombay Presidency**. While it shared common goals with the **Brahmo Samaj** of **Bengal** and the **Arya Samaj** of **Punjab**, its approach was more **gradualist** and **moderate**.
 
• **Key Leaders:** Other notable members included **N.M. Joshi**, who later founded the **Social Service League** in **1911**, and **G.G. Agarkar**. These individuals contributed significantly to the **modernization of Indian society** in the **19th century**.
 
• **Literature:** The **Samaj** published journals and pamphlets to spread its message. The **Subodh Patrika** was a weekly journal published by the **Samaj** to educate the public on **social and religious issues**.
 
• **Comparison with Brahmo Samaj:** While the **Brahmo Samaj** broke away from **orthodox Hindu traditions** more radically, the **Prarthana Samaj** leaders preferred to remain as **social protesters** within the existing **religious structure**.

questions.question:
In this question, a question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer.

Q. Five friends – Gaurav, Himanshu, Ishan, Lokesh, and Mukul – are of different ages.

Who is the third oldest?

(I) Ishan is older than Gaurav but younger than Lokesh.

(II) Mukul is older than Ishan but younger than Lokesh.

options.text: Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement II is not
Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement I is not
Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question
Both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. Ishan is older than Gaurav but younger than Lokesh.

II. Mukul is older than Ishan but younger than Lokesh.

Analysis:

I. From Statement I → Lokesh > Ishan > Gaurav, but no information about Himanshu and Mukul → Not sufficient.

II. From Statement II → Lokesh > Mukul > Ishan, but no information about Gaurav and Himanshu → Not sufficient.

Using both I and II together →

From I: Lokesh > Ishan > Gaurav

From II: Lokesh > Mukul > Ishan

⇒ Combining: Lokesh > Mukul > Ishan > Gaurav

But, Himanshu’s position is unknown, so the third oldest cannot be uniquely determined.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper purchased 59 dozens of articles at the rate of ₹520 per dozen. He sold each one of them at the rate of ₹52. What percentage profit did he make?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit percentage is independent of the number of items sold (59 dozens).

CP of 1 article = 520 ÷ 12

SP of 1 article = 52

Ratio CP : SP = (520 ÷ 12) : 52 → 10 : 12 = 5 : 6

Profit % = (Difference ÷ CP unit) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ Answer = 20%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 

**Given:**

CP of articles = ₹520 per dozen

SP of each article = ₹52

Total quantity purchased = 59 dozens

**Formula used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
• CP (1 Doz) ₹520 SP (1 Doz) ₹624 
• 
 Profit: +₹104 Profit % = (104 ÷ 520) × 100 = 20% 

**Calculations:**

CP of 1 dozen articles = ₹520

⇒ SP of 1 article = ₹52

⇒ SP of 12 articles (1 dozen) = 52 × 12 = ₹624

⇒ Profit per dozen = 624 − 520 = ₹104

⇒ Profit % = (104 ÷ 520) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percent

Profit or Loss percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price (MP)

The price at which an article is labeled is called the Marked Price. Discount is always offered on the Marked Price: SP = MP − Discount.

Relationship between CP and MP

The ratio of CP to MP can be expressed as CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the single equivalent discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: Which type of touchscreen functions by pressing two flexible layers together, allowing it to detect input from a non-conductive object like a fingernail or plastic stylus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Resistive touch**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Resistive touch** screen is a sensor consisting of two flexible layers coated with a **resistive material** (usually **Indium Tin Oxide** or **ITO**) and separated by an air gap or **micro-dots**. When pressure is applied to the surface, the two layers touch, completing an electrical circuit and allowing the device to register the **location** of the touch. ***Hence, the description provided in the question matches the functionality of Resistive touch.***
 
• This technology is **pressure-sensitive**, meaning it does not require a conductive object (like a human finger) to operate; it can detect input from a **plastic stylus**, **fingernails**, or even **gloved hands**. ***Hence, the statement regarding non-conductive objects is correct.***
 
• The **Resistive touch** system is widely used in **industrial applications**, **medical devices**, and **point-of-sale (POS) terminals** because of its high **durability** against **dust** and **water**.
 
• It was one of the earliest touchscreen technologies, commercialized in the **1970s** after being invented by **Dr. G. Samuel Hurst** in **1971** (originally called the "Elograph").
 
• While cost-effective, **Resistive touch** screens generally do not support **multi-touch** gestures like pinching or zooming and have lower **image clarity** (around **75% to 80%**) compared to other technologies because of the multiple layers involved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Capacitive touch**:

 
 
• This technology uses a layer of **conductive material** (like **ITO**) that stores an **electrical charge**.
 
• When a **conductive object**, such as a human finger, touches the screen, it draws a small amount of **current** to the point of contact, creating a **voltage drop** that the **controller** processes as an input.
 
• It is highly **responsive**, supports **multi-touch**, and provides **high clarity**, making it the standard for modern **smartphones** (e.g., **iPhone**, **Samsung Galaxy**) and **tablets**.
 
• However, it generally does not work with **gloves** or standard **plastic styluses** because they lack **conductivity**.
 
 
 
• **Infrared grid touch**:
 
 
• This system uses an **X-Y grid** of **infrared LED** emitters and **photo-detectors** around the edges of the screen.
 
• When an object touches the screen, it **interrupts** the invisible **light beams**, allowing the **sensors** to pinpoint the **coordinates**.
 
• It is used in **large-scale displays**, **outdoor kiosks**, and **military applications** because it provides **100% light transmission** and **high durability**.
 
 
 
• **Surface acoustic wave (SAW)**:
 
 
• SAW technology uses **ultrasonic waves** that pass over the **touchscreen panel**.
 
• When the panel is touched, a portion of the **wave is absorbed**, and the **transducers** detect the change to register the **event**.
 
• It offers superior **image clarity** and **resolution** compared to resistive screens but can be affected by **surface contaminants** like **grease** or **dirt**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of Features**: **Resistive screens** are preferred in **logistics** and **factories** (year-round use with **tools/gloves**), while **Capacitive screens** dominate the **consumer electronics** market (**year 2007 onwards**) due to the **user experience**.
 
• **Technical Limitations**: **Resistive touch** screens are susceptible to **scratches** because the top layer must be **flexible** (usually **polyester**) rather than **hard glass**.
 
• **Calibration**: **Resistive** panels often require periodic **re-calibration** to ensure the **software** correctly aligns with the **physical touch point** as the **flexible layers** age over **time**.

questions.question: The acid present in the atmosphere of Venus is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**H2SO4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The atmosphere of **Venus** is famously thick and toxic, consisting primarily of **Carbon Dioxide (96.5%)** and **Nitrogen (3.5%)**.
 
• The most defining feature of the Venusian atmosphere is its permanent layer of **thick clouds** composed of droplets of **sulfuric acid (H2SO4)**. These clouds are highly reflective, which is why **Venus** appears as the brightest object in the sky after the **Moon**.
 
• These **sulfuric acid clouds** are located at an altitude of **45 to 70 kilometers** above the planet's surface. The concentration of the acid in these droplets is estimated to be between **75% and 96%**.
 
• The formation of **sulfuric acid** on Venus occurs through **photochemical reactions**. In the upper atmosphere, **ultraviolet radiation** from the **Sun** breaks down **carbon dioxide** and **water vapor**, which then react with **sulfur dioxide (SO2)** to create **H2SO4**.
 
• Unlike **Earth**, where clouds are made of **water vapor**, the environment of **Venus** is extremely caustic due to the high concentration of this **mineral acid**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Planet Characteristics:** **Venus** is often described as **Earth's twin** because of its similar **mass**, **size**, and **composition**. However, its atmospheric conditions are vastly different and hostile to life.
 
• **Runaway Greenhouse Effect:** Because of the high **carbon dioxide** concentration, **Venus** experiences a **runaway greenhouse effect**. This makes it the **hottest planet** in our solar system, with surface temperatures reaching approximately **467°C (872°F)**, which is hot enough to melt **lead**.
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure:** The **surface pressure** on **Venus** is immense, measuring about **92 times** that of **Earth**. This is comparable to the pressure found at a **depth of 1 kilometer** under **Earth's oceans**.
 
• **Retrograde Rotation:** **Venus** is unique because it rotates on its axis in the **opposite direction** (retrograde) compared to most other planets. A **day** on **Venus** (243 Earth days) is actually longer than its **year** (225 Earth days).
 
• **Volcanic Activity:** **Venus** has a surface covered with **thousands of volcanoes**. It is believed that **volcanic outgassing** is the primary source of the **sulfur dioxide** that maintains the **sulfuric acid** clouds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Virga Phenomenon:** While it "rains" **sulfuric acid** in the upper layers of the Venusian atmosphere, the heat near the surface is so intense that the droplets **evaporate** before they can touch the ground. This phenomenon is known as **virga**.
 
• **Chemical Formula:** The correct answer **H2SO4** represents **Sulfuric Acid**. The other options provided in the question represent:
 
 
• **HNO3**: Nitric Acid.
 
• **HCl**: Hydrochloric Acid.
 
• **HCOOH**: Formic Acid.
 
 
 
• **Exploration History:** Several missions have studied this atmosphere, most notably the **Venera series** by the **Soviet Union** and the **Magellan** orbiter by **NASA**. The **Venera 13** probe was the first to send back **color images** of the surface in **1982**, surviving for only about **two hours** in the extreme conditions.
 
• **Phosphine Discovery:** In **2020**, researchers reported the potential detection of **phosphine gas** in the clouds of **Venus**, which sparked debates about the possibility of **microbial life** existing within the **sulfuric acid** layers, although this remains unconfirmed.
